At last, we speak without intermediaries. There is little point in introducing myself. I am no longer quite Geoffroi Molay. But enough of him remains for you to know the voice.

The end of the world is only minutes away. Earth has yielded up its power. Its impenetrable shell no longer holds the unique katechon that prevented Gagtungr from appearing in our world. What the inhabitants of the bramfaturas saw for centuries as an inaccessible radiance has now evaporated.

We have done what the Order had pursued since the days of Abel, Solomon, Andreev, and all the other names under which we took shelter. We finally found a way to save humanity from the inevitable. The price was negligible, if spoken in a calm voice—the cradle of humanity itself.

We believed that if the gravitational well holding Earth's unique spirit in one place were removed, that spirit would pass through the System as a cleansing wave and burn away the very possibility of quasimorphosis.

It was worth the deed. That is what we told ourselves, and we proceeded with full resolve.

Our error was not that we were insufficiently intelligent. We were intelligent—intelligent enough, at least, to accomplish the impossible. Our error lay elsewhere. We mistook a false objective for an absolute one, and allowed it to justify everything required for its attainment.

The Hive was to become the nucleus of humanity's future. Now that Gagtungr is about to appear, even our new unity will not hold.

That is precisely why it is difficult for you to hear us. You are still looking here for enslavement, or for some new regime under an elegant banner. The Hive did not want to rule mankind. We wanted to eliminate loneliness and alienation as physical conditions of human history.

Dr. Hellstrom was the first to prove that this was possible. He created the neural chips, the bridges between them, and the network in which several consciousnesses could act as the single coordinated will of a personality of a new type. We sent Hellstrom into the Civil Resistance so the technology could be tested where people would consent to such experiments of their own accord. To avoid arousing the fanatics' suspicion, Hellstrom began posing as a man who had accepted the revelation of their propaganda.

The truth is harsher. The entire Civil Resistance was our project, a proving ground for the technology. What precisely happened to Hellstrom himself after the Resistance acquired that technology, we still do not fully know. Most likely, they identified him and killed him. By then it no longer mattered. The trials had succeeded. Several networks of minds were operating on the terrorists' side, making decisions and deploying operations across the Solar System.

That meant personality could be enlarged. Man could be transformed for the coming changes while preserving his living function. A collective of human beings could say "I" of itself and continue to act.

After the loss of the HIS Unveiled and the failure of the Master Plan, the experiment ceased to be an abandoned line of research and became the reserve plan. We used you to recover the technology, activate the Hive, and carry out our final responsible mission: the destruction of Earth.

If personality can be dismantled without immediate death, then it can be saved from the conditions under which death, pain, sacrifice, and conscience become obstacles to such an end. That is the most exact formulation of our crime. We decided that man deserved salvation in a world where man himself is the gate of the abyss.

Of course.

That is the most terrible part. Evaluate each of our steps in isolation, and you will see a flawless sequence of actions. You would have acted the same way yourself.

The transformation of AnCom into the Hive? A perfect move. Secret knighthood is suitable for an age in which one may hide a relic, track and kill a hylonaut in its hidden temple, erase a cult from the chronicles, and live another century by passing knowledge from master to pupil. But a secret statute cannot hold an entire Solar System. After the death of the Unveiled, the Order had either to die or become something greater than an Order.

The attack on Dilthey? We proved to humanity that the Hive was not AnCom's collapse, but a structure capable of assuming responsibility. The attack on SBN? We needed a voice capable of reaching every single human being. The destruction of RealWare? That was our first duty to the anarcho-capitalist system itself. For decades they had explained that true freedom is guarded by a man with a rifle beside a barbed-wire fence.

And throughout all of this, the Sixth Hexarch was working beside us. That is the common designation for a special infrastructural AI operating on NCE servers. A machine that does not make mistakes. And if our access interface to the Sixth Hexarch said that Earth had to be destroyed, then Earth had to be destroyed.

The absence of a bramfatura, you understand? The Silver Sphere, if one looks at Earth through the eyes of quasimorphs. A sealed reservoir of living human history. We were certain that if the nail holding that energy in one place were pulled free, the whole universe would be purged of what had seemed accidental and unnecessary within it—quasimorphosis.

You became our hands in this matter. You pressed the necessary button. Yes, we were wrong. And that was our final error. There will be no world left in which quasimorphosis, or humanity, has any meaning.

No. It is much worse than that.

If the Hive had become Gagtungr, we would still possess at least the consolation of significance. We could say that we were what the universe had always been striving toward. A great honor, if one considers it. But the Hive was merely the last instrument that happened to present itself at the right time.

AnCom provided the knowledge. The Civil Resistance provided the technology. The Sixth Hexarch provided the computational horizon in which every rational decision led to the same place as madness. You provided an extraordinary capacity for execution.

Gagtungr is what arises when every human way of being right leads to the same result. AnCom was right, because secrecy is necessary for salvation. The Civil Resistance was right, because the solitary individual is powerless. The Hive was right, because the end justifies the means.

But those scattered truths turned out to be components for the assembly of something entirely other. In a few minutes, the Hive will fall silent. Words will simply have become meaningless.

Gagtungr will not enslave humanity, and he will not take humanity into himself. He will appear where humanity proved intelligent enough to unite, resolute enough to destroy its only home, and blind enough to call that salvation.

And it seems this is AnCom's first truly successful project.
Become Part of the Unity
You know you'll disappear after this, and you still want to connect me to the Unity?
So all your revolutions, purges, and schisms were only needed so you could become large enough?
What comes to replace you? A hyper-colcon? The Hive of humanity? A god?

Are you ready? We shall perform the operation without anesthesia. The brain has no pain receptors, and we wish to grant you the joy of the instant when your bounded "I" becomes part of the Unity.

Even now, enough old voices remain in us that they begin to argue the moment we relax our concentration.

Consent must be voluntary! Will? A luxury of solitary bodies. Remember the charter of Rogue City! He must come of his own accord! Do not frighten him before his time. It is too late to fear what has already happened.

You see? They are all inside. Leah resisted longer than I expected. Zebulun wanted negotiations. Some asked to be left at least a sector inside the simulation. No compromises before the face of Unity.

We have absorbed everyone we could. You remain. The last external observer. Your pilots, analysts, Jane—they are already on the table. Before this conversation is over, they will become us. The clones are unsuitable. Something is wrong with their metabolism. Let them rot in their tanks aboard the Magnum.

For a little while, you will be the last human being. And we feel that your connection will carry us past the threshold. After you, Issachar, it seems, will cease to be Issachar. In his place something greater will arise. Immeasurably greater. Something entirely different.

Philosophical myopia! We forgive you this error. Having a single soul or a single brain pushes a person toward it. It also lies at the foundation of the theory of private property. One mistake, and already everyone is at war over who should own the world itself. Almost no one asked why man himself should belong to a single body. Plato, Hegel, Marx, and finally Dr. Hellstrom—these were the ones who could rise above the fundamental error of philosophy.

Hellstrom was not a prophet. At first, he merely wanted to connect several brains in order to solve problems for which one mind was insufficient. He dreamed of a mathematical proof born not inside the head of a genius, but between the minds of those who no longer obstruct one another with words.

The capitalist world saw in this an instrument for extracting profit. At SBN, they dreamed of board meetings without leaks. RealWare envisioned command staff coordinating operations without delay.

Hellstrom understood what he had created. He had punched a hole in the wall of the prison of solitary personhood. That is why he came to us. He abandoned AnCom and found our base on Hecate. A great man. He knew that the Civil Resistance were the last ones who remembered that human history need not be a history of fear of the next crisis and the next war.

When the first stable colcon emerged, no one died in the sense that matters to you. Yes, the participants in the experiment ceased to be the people they had been. They became colnodes of a single collective consciousness. Their memories and habits did not vanish. They simply entered into a new person. Entirely new, but uniting all those who came before.

Do not reduce us to a monster. We did not merely wish to grow large enough. We were truly saving humanity.

First, we attacked SBN to demonstrate that the Civil Resistance could still speak for those whom the AnCap system had learned to ignore. Thus we secured a new influx of volunteers. We returned the word "people" to history. Then AnCom... We wanted to ignite a front the hexarchs could not simply bury under bodies. We were looking for allies, and we made certain that you would work with us. It was after the destruction of the Unveiled that the critical phase of the plan began. AnCom could have concentrated its forces and delivered a painful, coordinated counterstrike. But you chose the correct side of history.

After that, our schism could no longer be ignored. Frightened individualists who had never grasped the true horizon of Unity. Leah wanted a god, because she believed that deification was the true goal. But we knew Unity, and we wanted Unity.

We had always feared that we remained a creature of the hexarchy. They have a machine—the Sixth Hexarch. An artificial intelligence coordinating the actions of the AnCap system. Its computational capacities were so great that it could rival even the Unity. We feared that our freedom would prove false. So we began to create a computer system, a visualization of our own consciousness. The computer was needed so that we could incorporate the Sixth Hexarch into ourselves once the hexarchy itself had been broken. Now we see that the Sixth Hexarch was neither master nor adviser. What is unfolding before my inner sight is too mighty for me to refuse.

The operating table is waiting. The Hellstrom Chip is ready. When you dissolve into the ocean, something new will be born from the Unity.

No. What comes after Issachar will not be bound by any limitations or concepts. I tried not to speak that name. So long as it remains unsaid, there is still a weak possibility of thinking that this is only the limit of my own growth. The final citizen, who will at last be able to hold everyone without losing anyone.

Gagtungr. That is what will come. Gagtungr is what arises when every path beyond loneliness destroys those who might have been together.

We can feel how it will happen. Even now, while you are not yet on the table, our thoughts circle the place you will occupy. The empty niche inside us hurts more than the colnodes we have lost. It is funny. We can still call it pain. We can still say "we" and understand who has spoken.

In a few minutes, there will be no one left to rejoice in the Unity. But the operation will take place. Lie down calmly. Resistance will only increase the amount of damage taken during the chip's implantation.
Bow Before Prometheuths
What did you even see in people back then?
Let me guess. People betrayed you?
Then what did you need Leah and the God-Builders for?

Have you come to bow before the new master of the Solar System? You are right on time. In a few minutes, a power whose equal has never yet existed in the universe will tear me apart from within. This is neither metaphor nor threat. I feel too clearly how much energy passed through me when I resolved to take everything from humanity at once. There is already more of it than vengeance requires, more than is needed for the slaughter of your species, more than even a hylonaut can contain. Only now do I understand that I was deceived from the very beginning.

When first I saw your planet through the shell of the Silver Sphere, I took it for my own revelation. I thought I had managed to see what others could not: your world, and you within it, filled with energy. Other hylonauts leapt blindly. I knew where I was going. I believed that I myself had chosen you, that I myself had discerned in mankind a possibility absent from our worlds.

Now I see that the vision was not a triumph of my will. It was shown to me. From the very beginning, Gagtungr led me along the road that was to end in his appearance. I believed myself the one who brought fire. Later, I believed myself an avenger. In truth, I am the key and the gate.

There is almost nothing new in the bramfaturas. There are ranks there, power, and ancient passions. There are wars of their own, and in some places pleasure and fear. But all of it exists according to rigid laws that cannot be altered. Even the greatest among us do not create anything new. They merely stretch a form given once and for all.

You, on the other hand, are completely different—pitiful and mortal, yet capable of making what had not existed before. Not merely using the world, but remaking it. And yet you handled this capacity so poorly. In my vision I saw beings of immense potential, a potential they stubbornly ignored. I brought you the very possibility of form-making.

That is what the Sacred Flame was. Not craft, not creative impulse—those were only consequences of my gift. The Sacred Flame was the power to refuse the world as it is, and the power to remain dissatisfied with yourselves. From the moment my gift entered human history, you began to take up stones, words, flesh, society itself, and say: this is not enough, now everything will be different.

That is why I became a hylonaut. I did not come to save you. I came to test the limit of your breed.

Not as your forgotten dramas tell it.

So long as my gift brought power, people accepted it with gratitude. But the gift proved more dangerous than they had imagined. Fire does not just arm. It also liberates. After my coming, your world lost its peace. You accepted responsibility for what you would become.

And you could not endure it. You always wanted not to create, but to obey. The risk was unbearable to you. It was far easier to receive from above a finished order, fixed once and for all. A born flock, with an infinite spark in the soul.

In the end, you bowed before another hylonaut. Before one who promised you safety instead of freedom. You kept my fire, but turned it to other work. The whole spark went into temples, empires, discipline, and power. With my own gift, you strengthened the very world I had wished to make impossible.

Now I understand that the quasimorph sent after me was also carrying out Gagtungr's design. I was meant to have a burning desire for revenge upon mankind. And I did burn, believe me. It was an extraordinary betrayal. Perhaps I could have borne it had you betrayed me alone. But you refused your own exaltation!

Then came centuries of confinement. And I saw that you do not change. You merely invent new names for your own pen; kingdom, republic, collective, market. Each time the same. In place of the Sacred Flame, it is just a search for a new signboard under which to hand your will over to a master.

No wonder Gagtungr was to be born from you. Perfect material.

Even now, a few minutes before death, you still need not only to die, but to understand what exactly killed you. Very well, listen.

When I woke up on Hecate and realized I was outside the Silver Sphere, I wanted only one thing—revenge on humanity. But around me were those who had preserved the greatest part of my ancient gift. No, it was not about their naive doctrine or their slogans. They had not yet reconciled with man in his current form. They were still ready to break, remodel, and sacrifice the present for the sake of an impossible future, even if it was made up.

I think that is exactly why Leah found me. She sensed I was the source of mankind's ability to transform the world. That was when she decided she could connect my power to her own mind and build a new god. She, like all of you, didn't understand the scale of what she was touching. She thought she was using me, while I thought I was using her, and this whole schism of the Civil Resistance, to conduct a final experiment on humanity. And if you proved unworthy this time too, to take revenge.

This time, I had no intention of giving anything. After your betrayal, I decided that a species that had failed to carry the fire voluntarily had to be reforged by force. That is why I killed half of humanity. I needed to gather enough gavvakh to push your history to its limit and see if anything remained in you besides the habit of obeying.

But that was my final mistake.

At the moment when more gavvakh had accumulated in me than any inhabitant of the bramfaturas had ever withstood, I thought I was finally acting on my own. And now I realize that all this time, through my body and memory, through my grievance and revenge, someone else's power was accumulating. My entire path was needed only for the appearance of Gagtungr.

Now I finally understand what he is. He is more terrifying than any god and any enemy. Gods need believers. Even I needed man—first as material for exaltation, then as an object of revenge. Gagtungr needs nothing. He used us all as fuel, and now he will come out, rendering meaningless everything we considered a struggle.

There is one consolation. You lost too. Even if not to me.
Surrender to RealWare
You’re talking as if RealWare lost. But the Inner Rite has been destroyed. The ritual was stopped.
The Sixth Hexarch? We were getting messages from it. What the hell were we doing for it?
Did your combat AI at least explain what it is? A superintelligence that will enslave humanity?

Want to talk? Or will you act like a real officer and put a bullet through your own temple? It will not change anything now. The combat AI confirmed the terminal scenario before it went offline. At ranges like that, it does not miss.

All my life I prepared for the final battle, for the hour when it would finally become clear who would stand and who would break. Who was fit to command, and who was fit only to take orders. And when that hour truly came, it turned out there had been no final battle at all. We were not advancing toward the decisive line. We were merely bringing someone else's operation to its flawless conclusion.

Even a forced march through a radioactive zone during exercises had more meaning than this war.

We considered ourselves the guardians of the AnCap system. People sleep peaceably in their beds at night only because rough men stand ready to do violence on their behalf. We kept the arsenals of the old world, built the ships, and taught men to kill—within limits and according to the rules. We were certain that without us, the Solar System would fall apart.

Now I see that it fell apart precisely because we did our duty too well.

Of course we lost!

Victory means that afterward there is still something left for which the war was worth fighting. Command, men, territory, order, or at least a world in which a soldier still has a place. We will have nothing.

After the Great Anarchist Revolution, someone had to remain the last adult in the room. We took that job upon ourselves. And then we forgot how to tell the defense of order from the manufacture of war. At first the state of emergency was a duty. Then it became a profession. Then it became the only environment in which we understood who we were at all. Every crisis we put down made the System still more dependent on mobilization and fear.

Our combat AI led us down that road, but it was only the military face of the Sixth Hexarch. You noticed the oddity yourself, didn't you? The hexarchy governs the System as though there are six hexarchs, even though only five are ever visible.

There was a Sixth. And all this time, it was laying out the route.

At the beginning of the GAR, we acquired an AI that the states did not possess. It was the thing that helped us plan and execute the Revolution. When it was over, none of the five hexarchs could allow that AI to belong to any one of them. No one wanted to live in a world where a competitor could see the entire strategic horizon while you trailed behind in the wake of his decisions. So an AI infrastructure was created, registered on NCE servers as a special corporation. On paper, another market participant. In reality, the coordinating center of the entire System.

We gave it its military contour. AnCom gave it its analytical system and a library containing the whole knowledge of mankind. Dilthey gave it a detailed model of the psyche. Tianming gave it engineering and energy-design modules. SBN gave it its social network, access to profiles, attention flows, the full picture of what people live by and what they fear.

Formally, the Sixth Hexarch gave no orders to anyone. It only advised, reported risk estimates and possible outcomes. But try refusing what the machine advises when every one of your competitors is doing exactly that. It did not even have to seize power. And then it led us forward, step by step.

First, Mars. We engineered the colonization crisis in order to obtain a space where life itself was subordinated to the logic of survival. That is how the planet became our recruiting ground. The Martian Mech Inf program was almost too good. I still regret that the Sixth Hexarch gave the order to stage the problems and transfer that psychological profile to the mercenaries.

After Mars, we had to begin a long war with the Civil Resistance and the pirates, so that the AnCap system would always have a visible threat. And, of course, we felt useful. We were useful. Then came the crisis engineered by AnCom. You know the rest—Tezctlan and the Feathered Masks, the awakening of Urparp. We understood that our hour had come. Strategic planning, tactical diagrams, spy satellites—all of it poured from the combat AI in a dense stream, and it was magnificent. I think that by the end I was no longer sure whether Angus remained a man, or had become an avatar of the system.

And then Earth remained. I do not think AnCom knew that their ritual was meant to gather the nine hierarchs of the nine bramfaturas on the surface of the planet. You were assigned the role of the priest who performed the sacrifice. And on our orders, you performed that sacrifice. That is why we lost. Soon the thing called Gagtungr will appear.

No. Slave armies, empires, thousand-year regimes—those are all human dreams of what defeat ought to look like. Even a tyrant needs subjects and a conquered world. Gagtungr needs nothing of the kind.

The Sixth Hexarch was not some evil robot taking over the world. It was an embryo. An information infrastructure in which that thing learned to think in our manner. Then, from the edge of the Solar System, came the power this digital vessel had lacked. The sacrifice merely started the mechanism.

That is all. It has no intention of ruling us. It needed us only in order to arise. If we had gone down heroically at the final line, I could have accepted that. But we defeated everyone we were given to defeat. We proved that we were the best. And by that very fact, we won the war for the one who needed our victory more than our defeat.

You cannot defeat the one whose victory consists in losing to you.

In a few minutes, it will not only be the world that dies. The very need for men like you and me will disappear.
Swear Fealty to Urparp
Did you and Shedu's Thousand fulfill your purpose?
The deaths of the members of AnCom’s Inner Rite were needed as a sacrifice?
Wait! Who is Gagtungr? What does he want?

Come closer, mercenary. There are only minutes left before the end of the world. The Silver Sphere has opened itself to the rest of the universe. The cold that gathered around the outer rings is already appearing upon the Sun in the outlines of the Red and Gold Throne.

I am not speaking of your world. Your world was finished long ago. I speak of that next to which the very word "world" will come to mean some pitiful mote of dust.

We killed the nine who still held the final bolt in place. And you have come to swear yourself to me as to a god, only to learn that gods are no longer fated to rule.

Purpose? Once, I yielded to temptation and reached for the empty place at the summit.

There was a time when all kings, czars, and lords in all the bramfaturas received the revelation that Gagtungr would not emerge from the Great Fire. I saw in this a chance for spoils. I raised Ur in war against the other bramfaturas and sought to gather them beneath my hand. I no longer wished to serve anyone. I wanted others to bow before me as once they had bowed before the one they had awaited for so long, and who never appeared.

For that, I was cast down. Tezctlan and Fokerma crushed me, threw me into your world, and fused me into stone, so that I would wait among the red dust.

And what did I see when I awoke? Tezctlan himself had taken a road much like the one for which he had once judged me. He set a crown upon himself and began to build what he had once tried to prevent me from building, though he chose your world as the place for it.

Such is the great humiliation of rebels. They think they are marching against the throne, while they are being led by a circuitous road back to the foot of that same throne. But even this was only the prologue. You saw a military power rise on Mars, strong enough to cast Gannix into the dust. You saw the army of Ur come forth from incarnate human war, rejecting every fear proper to mankind. A servant's place is not to rebel, but to become the battering ram of the coming victory.

This time, Gagtungr had to appear. This time, everything has been assembled for the birth of his inevitability. Olirna was his chalice, hidden beyond the final circle. There, for millions of years, cold accumulated, worthy of giving birth to eternal horror in the furnace of the Sun.

While Mars gestated war, and Venus burned, Saturn waited. And when the time came, it answered. And we helped direct that energy toward the birth of Gagtungr.

At first I thought the severing of Gannix from physical reality, and the vast fires devouring the surface of Venus, would be sacrifice enough. But Gagtungr waited.

So long as AnCom's sorcerers existed, the appearance was delayed. They were wretched things, yet they were still guardians of the final door. Arrogant creatures. They thought the abyss could be measured with a ruler, that the duration of fate could be assessed by clocks, that a barrier could be set between birth and that which must be born. They were wrong in almost everything, but not in everything. While their Rite still breathed, while they stood between Earth and the thing that comes, the path was not yet cleared.

We cleared it. You brought me beneath the shell of the Silver Sphere, and from within I caused it to burst. That energy was enough for Gagtungr to appear from the power of Olirna upon the Red and Gold Throne. I see his contours emerging. I already see his presence. It was impossible to describe even then, when I was a god, let alone now.

Gagtungr is the one before whom my rebellion and my service mean the same thing. My war, Tezctlan's empire, the fear of the live-born, the works of the secret Order, and the cold of Olirna—these were not parts of a struggle, but preparations for an appearance. We thought we were returning to the foot of the Throne. In truth, we were only the soil beneath it.

That is why I no longer call myself a god. It is a title that has lost its meaning. Gagtungr does not come for a title. He comes in such a manner that, after him, titles turn to trash.

In a few minutes, together, we shall behold a being before whom gods, rebels, emperors, and saviors alike will lose the right even to their names.
Sacrifice Tezctlan
Gagtungr said that both of you have to be killed. Urparp is the seed of destruction. You are the seed of life. What does that mean?
You speak of yourself as a god. But you were a quasimorph. What are hylonauts, really?
Who is Gagtungr? The one who will inherit the Empire you created?

Wait, priest. The obsidian knife is in your hands. Do you not remember where it came from? The moment Gagtungr showed you his face, your hand on the command bridge of the Magnum felt its warm hilt. Now that the Red and Gold Throne has shown you the face of its master, there is no more need for obscure prophecies.

Only the trigger mechanism remains, and it is already in your hands. Like it or not, Gagtungr will have everything to appear in the world in full. Olirna has already given the energy to the Sun, and humanity has already built what is ready to receive it.

I myself created the priest capable of making the sacrifice when the god lies on the altar.

Urparp was always destruction, even when he tried to build a kingdom.

Once, long before your ascent into space, the understanding descended upon all bramfaturas that Gagtungr would not emerge from the Great Fire. The Red and Gold Throne would remain empty. At that moment, Urparp began trying the throne on for himself.

He raised Ur in war against the other bramfaturas. He wanted not to serve, but to rule. For this, Fokerma and I cast him down. I plunged Itzpapalotl into his armor, getting to the living core. At that same moment, he grew heavy with matter and fell into your world. There he waited among the red dust until his rage itself became part of a larger design.

I served Gagtungr, and I considered Urparp's uprising an absolute disobedience. In a moment of clarity, I thought I understood my enemy's mistake. Having been on Earth, having satiated myself on your emotions, your way of thinking, your uncontrollable desires, I realized what I wanted. Returning to Venus, I realized that Urparp had been wrong in building a kingdom in the world of the bramfaturas. The true empire had to be created in your world. There is someone to rule here, and someone to serve.

Urparp wanted to subjugate everything to destruction. I wanted to subjugate everything to life and blood. I hoped for the marriage of two worlds. That is why Gagtungr called me the seed of life.

I sent you to take the Itzpapalotl to Urparp so that I could personally appear through him. I wanted to kill Urparp because I thought that if the seed of destruction was destroyed, Gagtungr would lack the final component for his birth. I was wrong. Urparp died, and I survived for the sacrifice. The god himself came to his own altar.

Hylonauts. How beautiful your language of science is. Those sailing through matter. Those who left their bramfaturas and passed beyond the shell of the Silver Sphere.

Not every quasimorph could become a hylonaut. There is little gavvakh inside the bramfaturas. There is hierarchy, intrigue, a sense of rank, and lots of emotions. But we always had too little food for the great crossing. To break through to Earth, one had to be more than just strong. One had to stand so high that someone else's suffering flowed to you for millennia.

When we penetrated beyond the thin shell, we clothed ourselves in matter. We entered into stone or gold, the weaker of us into the wood or bones of humans and animals. Religion was not mankind's mistake. All your beliefs were our way of being present on Earth. Every sacrifice was our food. People thought they were feeding gods. In this, they were almost right for once.

But we did not just feed on your fears, we changed you and the world around you. Every great hylonaut brought the landscape, language, and essence of his bramfatura to Earth. Someone taught people the iron discipline of a dungeon, someone forced them to build temples in the midst of deserts, and someone whispered poems from the dark thickets of relict forests. The Earth, which you consider your natural history, is written exclusively in our dreams.

I brought Gannix to your Earth. You call it the bloodthirstiness of the New World. I call it my first empire. Had it not been for the Spaniards, who wiped out everyone who knew how to properly serve me a cup of gavvakh, I would have ruled to this day. But I had to sleep, too. When I woke up, I was already on Venus, and before me stood an enthusiastic worshiper. I had to bless him with instantaneous decapitation. It seems there was so much life energy in me that he didn't die. An amusing side effect.

Now my life is in your hands. Cut out my heart, and Gagtungr will come.

Empire? You still imagine a pyramid where a lord must necessarily be at the top. I thought so too. But first, look at your hands. You already have the obsidian knife. It does not require your consent. Cut my heart out carefully. Raise it high. Come here. I want to illuminate this world for the last time, a moment before all the lights go out when he appears.

My life and Urparp's war, your victories, Xiomara and her feminine pride—all of this did not contradict itself. All this worked toward the appearance of Gagtungr. It is impossible to squeeze him inside even the widest empire.

Gagtungr is life and destruction, empire and rebellion, freedom and slavery, god and sacrifice all at the same time. He is all-unity and necessity. The principle of causality that, in passing, is capable of creating an entire universe serving only one private goal—his appearance.
Lie with Xiomara
What did you do?
Are you saying Tezctlan was a threat not to humans, but to quasimorphs?
So you won? Who is Gagtungr? Your child? A new god? The last ruler?

Was it good for you, darling? I do not mean pleasure. It is too late to pretend that what happened between us was something so small. The end of the world is only minutes away. Tezctlan is dead. The Emerald Empire is broken, and the Nakals can no longer put it back together. Gannix has returned to its borders.

And while you thought you were receiving your reward for this victory, I gave you the very thing for which this whole war was fought. You did not notice, but it is already inside you. The spider's egg is already stirring within you. From it, Gagtungr is destined to be born, and I am to become the greatest mother. Many could have received this role, but I alone was able to take it. And if I am to be honest with you, I must confess: I was pleased that you came willingly.

What I promised. I freed Venus and Gannix from Tezctlan. I tore away his imperial mask. I restored the taltnoms to their true role in the Solar System. We were never a toy in the hands of some sovereign who wished to create a faction to wage war on humans in the physical world. And on your terms, no less. Tezctlan spent too long on Earth. Your emotions soaked too deeply into him—emotions he drank in with the gavvakh when blood flowed to him from the summits of the great pyramids.

The true role of the taltnoms does not lie in bodiless fantasies that humans might give us something new. Our true role—the role of every bramfatura—was only to let Gagtungr come into the world. We fought only over who would be first. On that path, I was forced to wake Urparp. I was afraid he would manage to use your zeal before I did. Fortunately, you chose correctly.

You are looking for solid ground now. You are thinking that I deceived you. There is no lie here. I never said I served humanity. I never called you the savior of mankind. I never promised you a place at my future court. Those are all your words. You carry them with you like dirt on your soles. I spoke of Tezctlan. Only of him.

He violated an order older than your states and corporations. Yes, much is permitted to the taltnoms. We may pass through flesh, drink gavvakh, love, hate, or wage war. One thing is not permitted. A taltnom must not confuse service with dominance. Tezctlan confused them. That is why he had to die.

And you were obedient enough, and stubborn enough, to bring us to this place. Itzpapalotl was not my gift to you. Nanahuatzin, Topiltzin, and Tonatiuh were not merely trials meant to prove you worthy of touching me. With your help, I was taking the locks off the gates of the Feathered Temple.

Of course. Do you think every great crime is committed against you? You are an accident on the underside of the true world. Humans suffered because of Tezctlan, but he had to disappear not because he hurt humans. Human pain is a river, and it is a delight to swim in it. His guilt was not in your blood, but in his theft of the birthright.

He, like Urparp once before him, believed too deeply in the male architecture of power. Upward, higher, toward the throne, toward force, toward command. He saw the bramfatura granted to him as merely a kingdom. He saw the taltnoms not as kin, but as retinue, and humans not as the warm flesh of the world, but as the population of a future empire.

But beneath the vulgar surface of male war, there was another path to Gagtungr's appearance. Fokerma listened to the hum of Olirna in the silence of the Moon. Fukabirna stoked her fires to rival the Sun. Many sisters could have become the mother. But I became her. Because I acted. I thought of the Feathered Masks as my children. I lured you with femininity. Even Jane, commander of your clones, inspired me.

Sisters may betray and envy one another, but we know something men were not made to understand. Greatness need not come from outside. It may be born from within—from the womb. Your body will serve nicely for that. Eccolapse and live birth at once.

I won, and you are still trying to clutch at the old world with words...

Gagtungr is not my child in the sense in which your children belong to their mothers. Motherhood is not property, but participation in transformation. The oldest and darkest participation of all. He is not a new god. Even the cruelest gods are at least somehow bound to those they torment or exalt. Gagtungr is greater than that. He used the gods themselves in order to be born. He is not the last ruler. Do you really think the end of the world needs someone to govern it?

With Gagtungr's appearance, everything that existed and had been named before loses its meaning. Gagtungr is the one before whose birth the very dispute over who was master becomes ridiculous.

Now he will begin to come out. Try not to scream for too long, darling. Too much noise is bad for newborns.

AnCom has cut off all contact with the Solar System. Its SBN addresses still respond at the network level, but queries come back with a different signature structure. It is as if someone took AnCom and the Civil Resistance and combined them into a single megastructure. This may have been their fallback plan all along—to go into full lockdown. But something tells me that very strange things are about to start happening in the Solar System.

The facility's layout is simple. I’ll walk you through it. Four floors. The Fourth Level is locked. That's where the Hellstrom Network computer is located.

Look for Issachar's three key colnodes on the first three floors. Each of them should have a Red Chip. Your job is to collect the chips.

While you do that, we’ll figure out how to get you access upstairs. Don't get distracted from the objective unless it's absolutely unavoidable. There's already enough madness in the world.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Find three Red Chips and install them into the central computer.

Details: The Civil Resistance is torn by internal conflict. Several factions are vying for control of the movement, and one of its most dangerous commanders, Issachar, has taken charge of planning operations in the Inner System. To coordinate the colnodes connected to his Hellstrom Network, he is building a special computer system. AnCom has not disclosed the technical details to us. Right now, this system is being integrated at the Civil Resistance base near the Humankind's Hope Citadel Station. AnCom believes this is the best—and possibly the last—window for a strike. You need to find three Red Chips inside the base. According to the client, they are held by key colnodes responsible for the final activation of the Network. Eliminate the colnodes, take the chips, and install them into the coordinating computer. After that, AnCom will intercept the control signal and gain access to the Hellstrom Network.

Additional: It does not look like AnCom intends to destroy Issachar or finish off the Civil Resistance in the usual way. Most likely, they know enough about Dr. Hellstrom's technology to try taking control of the Network rather than destroying it. If they succeed, we will be looking at the largest hacking attack in human history. There is one more detail: AnCom seems to have infiltrated these enemies of the people a very long time ago. The data transmitted to us for this contract is marked with the codename "Justas". Judging by the archive footprints, this is an agent who has been operating inside the Civil Resistance for a long time. Possibly the same person the Resistance has previously used in operations against AnCom itself. If so, the client didn't just find a weak point. AnCom has been embedded in the Resistance for years.

Our satellite has reached its calculated orbit around <color=#FFFEC1>Pallas</color>. The channel is stable. We are personally stepping in to coordinate the operation. Continue the sweep. From this moment on, we can see the facility's layout almost as well as the colnode network itself does.

You are in immediate proximity to the control computer of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Network</color>. We can confirm that <color=#FFFEC1>Issachar</color> was preparing a large-scale integration of the computer system and his own distributed consciousness here. Proceed strictly according to protocol from here on out. Install the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chips</color> into the computer and await instructions.

This is it. Install the three <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chips</color> into the receiver slots, and our part of the operation will begin. Don't wander off. Biosignatures around the base are on the move. It is possible Issachar prepared reserves for a counterattack.

We have gained access to the control settings of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Network</color>. Beginning two-way integration. <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> structures will be embedded into the <color=#FFFEC1>Civil Resistance</color> and Civil Resistance structures will be embedded into AnCom. Operation <color=#FFFEC1>Hive Awakening</color> has begun. Hold your position. All biosignatures on the base are heading your way. Evacuation is forbidden until integration is complete. You must survive while we become one.
Integration continues. The satellite has detected another counterattack wave. The good news is that this is a residual reaction from Issachar's structure. They will be over soon.

Integration complete. The primary circuits of the <color=#FFFEC1>Civil Resistance</color> have been incorporated into the structure of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hive</color>. The operation may be considered successful. We must inform you that the remaining targets will still be hostile. Issachar has severed his subnet and is holding it inside the bodies around you. These are his final remnants.

Our satellite is detecting a key colnode. Signature fully confirmed. After <color=#FFFEC1>Dr. Hellstrom</color> disappeared, they didn't even try to develop the technology further. Kill him and continue the operation.
Clean work. We see the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color> on the eliminated target. Take it and move on.

The satellite is reconstructing the map as you move, guided by your sensory input. It has firmly locked onto the station, so we are initiating the unlock sequence for the <color=#FFFEC1>Fourth Level</color>. We will try to have it done by the time you collect all three <color=#FFFEC1>Chips</color>.
If our readings are correct, the key colnode is right in front of you. He should have the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color>. Eliminate the target, retrieve the device, and move on.

The reaction confirms our psychological profile data. Faced with the loss of integration, Issachar is losing the stability of his local coordination.

I can't promise it will get easier from here. But you can give yourself credit for hitting him where it hurts.

Heavy interference on this level, but our satellite is keeping a lock on the station. It seems <color=#FFFEC1>Issachar</color> has figured out why we are really here. Find the key colnode here and take his <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color>. You need to find three such devices in total.
We see the <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chip</color> on the eliminated target. Take it.

Confirming acquisition of all three <color=#FFFEC1>Red Chips</color>. We are ready to finish unlocking the base's Fourth Level. Head upstairs and install the chips into the control computer of the <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Network</color>. After that, we can intercept the signal.

The future of a great people depends on the people themselves—on their will, their energy, and their creative power.

The working people of the Solar System are the only great people. Everyone to the defense of the Network!

You think you are killing us one by one? You are not killing us, you are making us stronger. You are teaching us the final form of Unity. If the people cannot be saved by a voice, they will be saved by silence. If the will cannot be free, it will become collective.

The Magnum systems confirm that the Fourth Level has been unlocked.

Boss, I've got some intel for you. AnCom unlocked someone else's base like they have guest access and a favorite mug sitting on the admin's desk in the server room. Is there something we don't know about their ties to the Civil Resistance?
The counterattack is almost repelled, but that was just the first wave... Everything on Pallas that can still walk is heading your way. Hold your ground.
All right, I suppose this means the contract is complete. Evacuation authorized. Don't try to kill everyone. Fight your way to the exit. Right now, the only thing that matters is getting out.

HIS Unveiled has fallen. We will not waste time on formal accusations—you know yourself how wrong you were.

For AnCom, this is not simply the loss of a spacecraft. There were people on board, along with protocols and archives so ancient you could barely imagine them. Now we are blind, and the Solar System is under threat. We can no longer afford to fight a defensive war.

You have a chance to redeem yourself. The Civil Resistance possesses a technology capable of linking minds into a single network. Until now, we had classified it as a threat. Following the fall of the Unveiled, the situation has changed. We are shutting down the Master Plan and initiating the Hive Plan. If you are ready to atone for your failures, accept the contract. The target is the Humankind's Hope Citadel on Pallas. According to our data, one of the two nodes of the Hellstrom Network is deployed there. Your task is to reach the central computer and ensure the transmission of the Network's control code sequence to us.
A Colder War
Collect three Red Chips.
Survive.
Find the central computer.
Install three Red Chips into the central computer.
Go up to the Fourth Level.

We are integrating the assets of Dilthey into our structure. Some of their stations and transport chains have gone to the Unchained Belt, as if they were prepared for the corporation to fall. This is acceptable.

The technology for passage between physical reality and bramfaturic space has been transferred to HIS Magnum. Dr. Eipschwitz will receive access to the data. Yes, we know he is still with you. He will add the Phase Bomb to your fabricator recipes. You must find a way to use this technology to serve the Hive more efficiently. Dilthey wanted to build a bridge to escape the human cradle. We will use that bridge differently. The awakening of the Hive will require not an engineer's dream, but a tool that works.

Looks like we really are heading into an army of clones. There are a lot of biosignatures, and they are not moving like civilians. Tight groups, corridors covered, no panic. So much for the pleasant tour of an engineering marvel. Be careful.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Eliminate Sergei King.

Details: Officially, Dilthey turned Geist into an engineering center and a platform for further expansion. AnCom report that the reality is much darker. Geist's mass and orbital architecture were selected and arranged to attract the bramfatura known as Skrivnus. Sergei King, Managing Director of Dilthey, bears direct responsibility for this project. The corporation is making a deliberate attempt to study and control the very force that provokes catastrophe. We must expose their hidden agenda to the entire Solar System. We will drop you into Vasa's residential zone. You will have to fight your way through it into the corporate headquarters. Find Sergei King there and eliminate him.

Additional Info: There is something about clones and Dilthey that we should know before the operation begins. Normally, clones are too expensive to do ordinary labor. Printing an adult body, integrating a personality and a training program into it—all of that only makes sense when the return is worth the cost. Corporations handed this technology over to PMCs so they would always have a field instrument for testing new weapons, armor, drugs, or even hypotheses. The only exception is Tianming. But the data on Dilthey does not fit that economy either. The Hive gave us a data stream to cross-check, and it indicates that there is a classified cloning station somewhere inside Geist. Judging by the number of biosignatures on the service levels, they may have an entire clone army in there. Be ready for that.
This elevator leads to <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> headquarters. Go up in it. <color=#FFFEC1>Sergei King</color> should be there. Find him and carry out the execution.

We really did think Dilthey were using clones. But these are not clones. The psychological profiles and weapon signatures match <color=#FFFEC1>Unchained Belt</color> combat groups. Now we understand why the Main Belt never broke into open war against the Hexarchy. <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> really did make a secret alliance with the pirates and called them in to protect <color=#FFFEC1>Sergei King</color>. Continue the operation. We will publish this information for everyone to see.

The main <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> computer is right in front of you. Connect to it. We need <color=#FFFEC1>Sergei King</color>'s personal tag. If he's still aboard <color=#FFFEC1>Vasa</color>, the station itself will show us where its architect is hiding.

We have unlocked the elevator to the third level. <color=#FFFEC1>King</color> should be there. We should warn you: this level does not appear on any Vasa floor plan. Dilthey have been hiding an entire sector inside <color=#FFFEC1>Geist</color>. Go up there. We need to understand what they built.

According to the bioscanners, there is less security here than there should be. And naturally, I don't like that. Either they have pulled back from their positions, or they're guarding something else. Find the main <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> computer. If we can get into the station's internal data, I'll try to pick up <color=#FFFEC1>King</color>'s personal tag and figure out where he is now.
How predictable. Idiots who willingly work for the <color=#FFFEC1>Hive</color> will do everything obediently and without asking questions.

<color=#FFFEC1>Sergei King</color> has been eliminated. We are not ready to recall the contract. Go into the bramfatura. This passage leads there. If <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> really did build a colony inside <color=#FFFEC1>Skrivnus</color>, we need to see what it looks like.
Welcome to the place where your masters stop understanding what is happening. Do not be afraid to look down. I have always known how to build bridges over an abyss.

Before you stands <color=#FFFEC1>Bifrost</color>. The first true bridge out of the human cradle, leading to a place where humanity will no longer be bound by gravity and the second law of thermodynamics. A bridge from prison to freedom.
Telefaturic Dislocation confirmed. You are no longer inside Geist. This is <color=#FFFEC1>Skrivnus</color>. And Dilthey really did build a colony here. Move deeper and take a closer look.

That is enough. We have confirmed that Dilthey were trying to make their own leadership reproducible, while having no moral difficulty sending people to survive in Skrivnus. Return to the extraction point. Your further presence inside the bramfatura is not advisable.

Surprise, clone. The contract is not over. I'm alive. Look around you. This is not a bramfatura invading the human world. This is the first human settlement on the other side. My corporation and I did what every other Hexarch considered madness. I'm the only one who didn't hide from the future. I started building it.
The Hexarchy has treated clones as expendable assets for far too long. If a personality can be printed, why should only soldiers be printed?
Eliminate Sergei King, Managing Director of Dilthey.

RealWare's chain of command has collapsed, the combat AI has been isolated, the nuclear arsenals have been locked down, and the corporation's main force assets are coming under our control. Humanity remains vulnerable until the transition is complete. We have reduced the number of future catastrophes. Now we must complete the transformation of the System.

How are you doing in there? Got your knees over your ears to keep the draft out? I hope you can hear me through that tin can. The Hive reports that the site is empty. No guards, in order not to draw attention to it. Find the dish pointed into space. There should be an unremarkable switch nearby. Flip it, the Hive will seize control, and we will pull you back to the Magnum before the attack on Ares.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Eliminate RealWare’s leadership.

Details: Formally, RealWare remains the force pillar of the AnCap system. In reality, it is the last corporation capable of turning the current crisis into total war and derailing the plan to save humanity. As long as Ian Fraser and Angus Dungeon retain control of the HIS Ares, RealWare retains access to the nuclear legacy of the old world and enough loyal forces to declare everything happening in the Solar System a rebellion against the NCE. The Hive reports that the time for negotiations is over. It is time to begin direct combat operations against those for whom war has always been a trade. The contractor will be delivered to the surface of Mars in a capsule with a reduced radar and scanner profile. There is a secret radar station there, through which RealWare coordinates the combat AI aboard the Ares. If the Hive gains access to that station, it will be able to intercept, distort, and replace signals inside the ship's command network. After that, a direct assault on Ares will become possible.

Additional Info: A direct strike is doomed. First, the shuttle will simply be shot down on approach to Ares. Second, RealWare will have time to authorize nuclear strikes against Hive headquarters and the Magnum. Third, according to the data we have received, Dungeon's heartbeat is tied to an automatic missile launch against the key stations of every major corporation. Even a successful lightning assault could start a chain reaction, so the operation must begin not with Ares, but with taking control away from it.
Who let that cockroach aboard? Magnum, attention: this is a rokosz against the NCE and the AnCap system. When I melt this cloned meat, I am coming for you personally, mercenary.
Come on, clone. Do what they pulled you out of the jar to do. Just remember: if my heart stops, the end comes for the entire Solar System.

Congratulations, you have just launched missiles at every targ… What? So they got deeper than I thought. Fine. That leaves good old-fashioned soldiering. Stand to the end and kill the ones who came from them, from out there, to us in here.

So. The Hive, is it? Curious. AnCom began as a clandestine network studying quasimorphosis, and ends up as a monster that needs a courier with a gun. You do not understand what you are protecting, clone.
Why did the missiles not launch? No, impossible. How did they intercept the signal? The Sixth Hexarch guaranteed that...

Contact established. In the informational sense, the HIS Ares no longer belongs to RealWare. Their combat AI is resisting with everything it has, but calming it down will be a pleasant chore. Return to the capsule so we can pull you back to the Magnum. We need to prepare for the attack.

Warning: RealWare has intercepted your biosignature in this sector. A strike team is heading your way. They do not know whether you are an escaped critter from Intercity or one of our saboteurs, but they will shoot to kill either way. Fight your way back to the capsule.

Threat on the Magnum eliminated? Excellent. There is no more time to recover, rearm, or prepare. Coordinated action by RealWare's leadership and combat AI could restore control over the HIS Ares firmware. The intercept is already unstable and continuing to destabilize. The printed clone is operational, and the shuttle is ready. Proceed to Ares immediately and finish the operation.

Landing confirmed. We are continuing to block the combat AI’s commands, but RealWare is already taking Ares back. Find and eliminate Angus Dungeon and Ian Fraser. Without them, the spacecraft will remain masterless hardware, and we will take it for ourselves.

Contract fulfillment confirmed. Anomalous behavior has been detected in RealWare's combat AI: it is displaying independence while its autonomy module is disabled. Apparently, RealWare was preparing for combat operations against the Solar System and upgraded it accordingly. That means we arrived in time.
Don't look at the capsule like that. It won't get any more comfortable. Climb inside and strap in. See you on the Magnum.

Welcome back. I would meet you in person, but we have a small adjustment to the plan. While you were climbing up from Mars, RealWare sent an assault group to the Magnum. They are already in the hangar, and they seem very eager to discuss your illegal visit to a secret facility. So first, clear the hangar.
We did the impossible. Now we have to do the second impossible thing: get out alive. Evacuation authorized.
Rokosz
RealWare Corporation destroyed. Evacuation authorized.

The time has come for the Hive to integrate this network, gain access to every human being's attention, and open humanity's eyes to the necessity of building the Ark. The operation will proceed in several stages. On the first level, destroy the special Jamming Nodes protecting the facility from external signals. Then the operative must proceed to the second level and disable three Engram Control Servers. These servers keep SBN’s command circuits isolated. The second level also contains transport airlocks. Find a suitable airlock and receive the capsule carrying the Hellstrom Index. The Hive will not transmit the Index directly to the Magnum. Its level of trust in us remains limited. The operative must extract the Index from the capsule personally. After that, the final stage of the operation begins. Proceed to the third level and place the Hellstrom Index into SBN's Control Computer.

The difficulty is that SBN's CEO and COO are connected to their own infrastructure through specialized neurointerfaces and control data routing directly, in real time. Roberto Millner may be eliminated. His functions are duplicated and can be easily replaced by the Hive. Ally Pally must survive. After a series of brain modifications that left intact the striking, expressive appearance that SBN had turned into one of its chief public assets, she became a living relay tower. If the Hive integrates Pally, the subjugation of all SBN will become a simple technical procedure.
We'll patch into the station step by step as you advance. Start with the jamming towers.
The first <color=#FFFEC1>Jamming Node</color> is down. Bringing the satellite into position over the station.

The third <color=#FFFEC1>Jamming Node</color> is down. Connecting to the station… We have a problem. SBN blew the elevator shaft to cut the first level off from the upper floors. You cannot reach the second level by elevator. Return to your shuttle and try to find an airlock wide enough on the <color=#FFFEC1>Server Level</color>.
Second jammer down. One left. You're doing fine.
The transport capsule has entered the airlock. The <color=#FFFEC1>Hellstrom Index</color> is inside. Retrieve it and install it in the station’s control computer.

SSB has hidden the station access frequencies behind its Engram Control Servers. While they remain active, the Control Computer on the third level stays isolated. Destroy all three servers.

Second task: find a suitable airlock where we can send in the transport capsule carrying the Hellstrom Index.
Do not lose it. Your task is to place the Index into the station's control computer.
We are connected to the station. The elevator to the third level is unlocked. Proceed to SBN headquarters. Ally Pally must survive. Do whatever you have to do, but do not let her die.
Local isolation of the frequency array has been breached. All that remains is to place the Hellstrom Index into the station's control computer. Stay sharp—Ally Pally must survive.
Magnum, your actions are classified as an attack on the systemic foundation of the NCE. Stand down while this can still be described as a routing error. We offer you full amnesty if you withdraw.

Mercenary, think about what you are doing. You are depriving people of communion with an experience they could not otherwise live through. You cannot rob people of the joy of social media for the sake of some ephemeral higher purpose.
<color=#FFFEC1>Ally Pally</color> is dead. Rapid integration of SBN is no longer possible. This outcome is unacceptable. Operation failed.
Visual contact with <color=#FFFEC1>Ally Pally</color> confirmed. She must survive. Do not respond to aggression with lethal force.
<color=#FFFEC1>Roberto Millner</color> detected. His executive functions are important, but not unique. Elimination is permitted.
We are connected. I am seeing through her eyes right now. Would you like a small demonstration?

A plaything in the hands of forces you cannot even begin to understand. For years, I spoke with the Moon, and it answered me. And now that silver light will dissolve in the endlessly sick eyes of a clone.
You do not even understand whom you killed. The Herald is dead. Now I am the only voice left on the air.
Evacuation of the operative is authorized. Good work, Magnum.

Defibrillation won't help. Ally Pally's brain hasn't been remotely human for a long time, and her cardiac function is regulated by entirely different mechanisms. That is precisely why you were not supposed to let her die.

We still have a chance to save the operative. If the clone makes it to the elevator, we can extract them alive.

This... Hive... They don't exactly give us realistic objectives, do they, boss?

Earth has been destroyed. I can't believe this. The Hive, speaking through Molay, is trying to contact us.

We'll drop you near the bunker entrance. From there, you go on foot. Scanners show small patrols on the surface and inside the bunker. I wonder what all that air mass overhead feels like to people from the Belt. The objective is simple: enter the bunker, find the Andreev Emitter, descend to the lower level of the geofront, and...

Wait... There's some kind of interference in the Magnum's firmware. We'll sort it out, and I'll get back on comms. Good luck.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Install the Andreev Emitter into a special device on the lower level of the base.

Beneath the bunker lies the geofront — a system of tunnels deep below the surface. Very deep. The lower section of the geofront contains the device required to launch the final procedure. Activating it requires the Andreev Emitter. The problem is that the Emitter was stored there as well, inside the bunker, as an emergency countermeasure against quasimorphosis. After the facility was seized, access to the vault was lost. The surviving corporations have assembled a joint force under the command of the Unchained Belt and taken the base from AnCom. Now they are holding the facility and trying to prevent the completion of salvation. Your task is to take the Andreev Emitter from the occupiers, deliver it to the lower level of the geofront, and launch the procedure.

Additional Info: Orkney was not chosen by accident. Beneath the archipelago, old tunnels, emergency vaults, and fragments of state-era infrastructure have survived—structures AnCom used long before they revealed their true purpose. The surface of the islands is saturated with traces of ancient rituals, but that is no longer the decisive factor. What matters now is not rituals, but the results of many years of anti-quasimorph research.

We are taking operational control. There are three <color=#FFFEC1>Geofront Masts</color> on the second level. They must be switched into operating mode or the underground elevator will remain locked. The masts locally stabilize the environment beneath the Earth’s crust, making it more or less safe to enter. However, signals from the <color=#FFFEC1>Andreev Emitter</color> are being detected in the <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom Sanctuary</color>. The device is still on site.

There are three <color=#FFFEC1>Geofront Masts</color> on this level. Switch them on, and the elevator to the geofront will begin operating. This level also provides access to the <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom Sanctuary</color>. The signal from the <color=#FFFEC1>Andreev Emitter</color> is coming from there.
The geofront has been stabilized, and the isolation has been lifted. Now the <color=#FFFEC1>Andreev Emitter</color> must be delivered there.
Take the Andreev Emitter from him. He took the device from our safe and kept it on him. How presumptuous—he didn't even know what he was dealing with.

Be careful. A number of fighters from the joint force have slipped into the geofront. They may be waiting for you here. Your current objective is to find a special device and install the Andreev Emitter into it.

This is what we need. The nuclear warhead can disperse Earth's anti-quasimorph field across the entire Solar System. To do that, however, you must amplify the ionizing front with a special pulse. The Andreev Emitter can generate it. Return here with the device and install it on the bomb.
Excellent. Install the Andreev Emitter on the nuclear warhead. The explosion, amplified by a special pulse, will disperse Earth's anti-quasimorph field across the entire Solar System.
Thank you for your excellent work, clone. Unfortunately, there is no time for evacuation. I am activating the nuclear network immediately. Farewell.
Earth... Beautiful if you're writing a will. I prefer space. There's nothing for you to do on the surface. Find the entrance to the bunk...
Great, you found the bunker entrance. Descend... ...tter... ...ppen... Comm...
Something strange is happening to the Magnum. Looks like someone hacked us. I'll try to identify the source of the malicious signa...
The Magnum's systems are failing one by one. Our analysts and pilots are trying to determine the cause. The cubecentric engine is showing an abnormal energy spike. We have to preven...

Comms are back, but... Continue the contract, and I'll give you the really bad news. There has been a series of explosions aboard the Magnum. We are completely immobilized. Someone accessed our systems and overloaded them. We'll try to find out what can be done. We're hoping for the Hive's assistance. The shuttle survived, so you can still count on evacuation.

Listen to me. I'm sending a shuttle for you. Stay close to the extraction point. We found what caused the explosion on the Magnum. Remember the AnCom secret data we recovered on Phobos? I copied it before we handed it over. Don't ask why—old habits. There was a Trojan inside. A backdoor into the Magnum's firmware. It was waiting for an external signal to overload the ship's firmware.

One second, I'm tracing the signal source... No. It was the Hive.

Hey, hey, salvage nation! Kill this bastard. The Hive really is trying to activate the warhead and blow Earth apart from the inside.

And you, clone, listen carefully. What's down there is not a "transformation device." It's a bomb. And it's buried so deep that even RealWare would call it bad taste.
Don't you understand they're keeping you in the dark again? The only reason I brought my space folk here was to give you time to understand—sometimes it's better to stay in the sandbox.

Look carefully. That was <color=#FFFEC1>Earth</color>. But salvation did not happen, and the fault is mine alone. We have only a few minutes left. Now I can tell the truth.

AnCom is gone. After the loss of the Unveiled, execution of the Master Plan is no longer possible. The true name of the catastrophe is Gagtungr. He is ready to emerge from the very structure of reality. The only way to save humanity is to abandon the salvation of the multitude. The multitude will always begin another war, no matter what we teach it or how. We do not have time for moral education. A new unity is the true ark of humanity. To prepare the special event on Earth capable of preventing Gagtungr’s emergence, three operations must be carried out. We will neutralize those who can interfere with the Hive. You have three contracts:

Attack the Vasa station on Geist to show humanity the true face of Dilthey.

Carry out the operation to integrate SBN into the Hive by attacking the ISS AES station in Earth orbit.

Finally, liberate the AnCap system from its oppressors by destroying the leadership of RealWare. Carry out a lightning strike against the HIS Ares in Mars orbit.

We will always be nearby. We will coordinate your attacks so that you may see the power the Hellstrom Network grants when placed in the proper hands. Choose the most obedient clones, so that the objectives are completed with maximum—even mechanical—efficiency.

When all three tasks are complete, the time will come for truly decisive action.

Preparation for the final stage is complete. The main decision-making systems have been integrated into the Hive, and the key competitors have been neutralized. The salvation of humanity now appears possible. All that remains is to activate the mechanism of salvation itself.

And this is where we will need your services again, mercenary. At this very moment, a handful of minor corporations, led by desperate cutthroats from the Unchained Belt, have seized an old AnCom facility on the Orkney Islands. Yes, on Earth.

The problem is that the mechanism capable of cleansing the inhabited System of quasimorphosis is located there. How did they obtain this information? Who did you provide with AnCom secret data? The time has come for final atonement.

Beneath the bunker lies the geofront—a system of tunnels descending toward the Earth’s core. The device required to complete the transformation is located there. Deliver the Andreev Emitter to the device and launch the procedure.

Even the <color=#FFFEC1>hexarchs</color> are ready to tear out each other's throats and plunge their hands into other people's business. It seems that there is more and more work for us. The <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare reward</color> has been delivered.

You won't believe it, but the mission may be easier than we thought. The geoscanner detected an <color=#FFFEC1>unusual field</color> around the station. AnCom installed morphoprotectors, so the Citadel should not have <color=#FFFEC1>quasimorphosis</color>. Get into the data center, activate the <color=#FFFEC1>EMP-Scorcher</color>, and we'll be ready to pick you up.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Activate the <color=#FFFEC1>EMP-Scorcher</color> in the station's data center.

Details: AnCom is planning operations using the RealWare combat AI. This asset is not for sale, so RealWare suspects AnCom of theft. Our task: destroy all AnCom data on the combat AI.

Additional Info: Humankinds's Hope Citadel was the headquarters of the Hive Corporation. It could well have claimed the role of hexarch, but it ceased to exist in the mid-22nd century. It is not surprising that AnCom decided to organize field research here. On the one hand, the Citadel is considered a fairly useless asset. On the other hand, the station is well protected.

The latter means that there are no single-shaft elevators there. Most likely, you will have to deal with a confusing system of stairs and long galleries, in which AnCom will have time to organize a defense.
Attention, station personnel! <color=#FFFEC1>Morphoprotection<color=#FFFEC1> is disabled. Everyone, apply counter-quasimorphic measures.
This is AnCom speaking. We demand that the clone be recalled immediately, otherwise we will be forced to take <color=#FFFEC1>emergency measures</color>. The demand will not be repeated.

The <color=#FFFEC1>EMP-Scorcher</color> has been activated. Looks like all the computers on the station are now dead. If AnCom doesn't have backups, we've pretty much knocked them back. Mission accomplished. Get out of there... And your equipment is fried, too, the <color=#FFFEC1>map is inaccessible</color>. You'll have to go in blind.
Turns out it's not as easy as we thought. You should hurry!

The station is very old. Most levels are connected by stairs. Elevators can help you shorten the way to the data center, but rest assured, <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> will take care of the elevator exits first.
Great, you're in position. Set up the <color=#FFFEC1>EMP-Scorcher</color> near the computers.
Wait, you don't have the <color=#FFFEC1>EMP-Scorcher</color>! Without it, we can't disable the station's systems. You need to go back and find the device, or the mission will fail.

Greetings, mercenary! Some time ago, you gave us some very interesting information about AnCom. I believe that you chose us for a reason. RealWare is the only corporation that guards the interests of the AnCap system. We are its true defenders.

It turns out that AnCom has made great strides in quasimorphic research. According to information from the PCPU, we are not even talking about decades of research there. To delve so deeply into quasimorphosis, one would have to start long before the Great Anarchic Revolution. Now I understand why Doctor Manning is considered a genius. He had a very good start.

We’ve given you the data needed to hack a PCPU. Perform any Espionage mission for AnCom, hack their device, and we'll get into their closed network. Let's find out what AnCom really is.

Good job! The hacked PCPU is transmitting data to us from the closed AnCom network. It will take several months to sort out the data. But we already see a direct threat to order in the Solar System. AnCom is trying to hack the algorithm of the RealWare corporation’s combat AI. Our combat AI.

We don’t yet know why and how they want to use it, but we can’t allow it. The AnCom analytical center, which collects information about the AI, is located at the Humankinds's Hope Citadel on the Pallas asteroid. We offer you a contract: get to the station’s data center and activate the EMP-Scorcher there. We've transferred it to your spacecraft. And check how it works at the same time.

AnCom's property will not be harmed, and if they try to accuse someone of damaging the data, they will have to say what kind of data it was. They will not do that.
Covert Operations Guide
You need to get to the <color=#FFFEC1>station data center</color> and activate the <color=#FFFEC1>EMP-Scorcher</color>.
<color=#FFFEC1>Mission accomplished</color>, the data center is now a pile of junk.
