<color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color> has been destroyed. <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color> is assuming control of the assets seized by <color=#FFFEC1>Shedu's Thousand</color>. Remaining pockets of resistance are being suppressed as a matter of routine. Command reports that the corporation's next strategic objective is to establish observational control over <color=#FFFEC1>Earth's</color> orbit. The time has come to declare, once and for all, that the achievements of the <color=#FFFEC1>Great Anarchist Revolution</color> have been saved—and to personally ensure that there will be no further failures in the AnCap system.

<color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color> is entrenched deeply enough in physical reality to exert control over the atmosphere of <color=#FFFEC1>Mars</color>. Everything that approaches the fortress too closely is burned out of the sky. So we will not be able to drop you right at the entrance. We will drop you where we can, and you will walk from there. The moment your boots touch the ground, you are considered a written-off asset. But not every clone gets the honor of throwing a phasonuclear charge into the face of a creature that so enjoys calling itself a god. Good luck, and goodbye.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Throw the phasonuclear charge at <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color> from close range.

Details: RealWare does not forgive traitors. A significant part of Shedu's Thousand consists of former corporate soldiers who abandoned discipline and chose the path of technobarbarians in the service of the quasimorph Urparp. Now it is time to collect on that debt. Using Eipschwitz's research, RealWare has created a new munition—a tactical phasonuclear charge, capable of damaging not only physical structures but quasimorphic entities as well. The device has already been delivered to the Magnum. You will need to take it with you on the mission. According to calculations from the RealWare combat AI, the only way to destroy Urparp for good is to bring the charge to a minimal distance from the target. In other words, you will have to literally throw the bomb at Urparp. Important! Extraction of the operative is impossible by design. Detonation will occur immediately once the charge reaches the target. The operation is strictly a one-way trip. The operative is considered an expended asset from the moment it begins.

Additional Info: Shedu's Thousand has turned the Sinkhole Oasis into a fortified zone. Before reaching Urparp, the clone will have to fight his way to this fortress alone.

You heard that? Don't hang around there. The mission is considered complete only once <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color> is destroyed. What we need is a finished contract, not a pointless slaughter one step away from completion.
That's it. The elevator goes down to <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color>. Once you get there, you'll have no other tasks left.
Urparp has been destroyed. RealWare confirms successful contract completion. Extraction authorized. Since you're somehow still alive, there will be more work for you soon.

Analysis complete. A direct channel into <color=#FFFEC1>Ur</color> has been opened on the surface. Every enemy you kill is immediately pulled by <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color> out of the bramfatura and thrown back onto the battlefield. New mission parameter: clearing the drop zone is impossible.
Something is wrong. We are detecting an anomaly in the quasimorphic data coming from the reconnaissance satellite. Initiating deep analysis. Continue the mission.
First lockout circuit deactivated. Nuclear weapons are now available for manual release from the craft. Nuclear strike readiness: twenty-five percent.

NCE lockout deactivated. Readiness one hundred percent. I am authorizing the strike on the Sinkhole Oasis. Time to execution: immediate.

The Sinkhole Oasis has been destroyed. We are registering a weakening of Urparp's phase-link to reality. Find him and kill him.

Good. You are still alive. <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color> vanished from <color=#FFFEC1>Mars</color> and appeared aboard the <color=#FFFEC1>Ares</color>. The spacecraft's structural frame will begin to fail very soon, and all attempts to kill the quasimorph by conventional means have proven ineffective. Just before it burned up, the reconnaissance satellite transmitted a new batch of quasimorphic data. Analysis complete. There are four special signatures in the <color=#FFFEC1>Sinkhole Oasis</color>. Destroy them, and Urparp's link to reality will weaken enough for him to be killed. There is no time for a ground operation. The Oasis will be destroyed by a nuclear strike. But under <color=#FFFEC1>NCE</color> requirements, the launch is locked. There are four authorization terminals on this level. Activate all of them. Once that is done, we will incinerate the <color=#FFFEC1>Sinkhole Oasis</color>.

Deactivation of the third lockout circuit confirmed. <color=#FFFEC1>NCE</color> restrictions have been lifted for emergency release of nuclear charges. Nuclear strike readiness from HIS Ares: seventy-five percent.
Please refrain from throwing the nuclear bomb around carelessly. The charge is inactive. Combat mode will be enabled only upon confirmed delivery to <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color>.

Shedu's Thousand has been eliminated. The attempt to turn Mars into a new staging ground for the quasimorph war has been thwarted.

RealWare has once again proven that it remains the only entity in the Solar System capable of resolving such crises at an acceptable cost. All others either create threats or become their fodder.

Now begins the truly important phase. Our next objective is to secure a foothold near Earth. Control over near-Earth space will allow RealWare to complete its force deployment in the theater where the fate of the entire Solar System will be decided.

We have a signal! Yes, yes, we are catching the clone's signature. He's alive! Listen carefully, I've opened a telephaturic passage for you to the <color=#FFFEC1>HIS Ares</color> of the <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color> corporation. Don't just stand there. Jump. I have no idea how long I can hold this hole open.

So this is how RealWare hoped to kill a god. With a spark drawn from the bones of the world.

Naive. The weapon in your hands is only a shadow of what was created in Ur. The fire with which you go to war is only a glimmer of the fires of Ur. Explosion, decay, tamed death—all of these are mere imitations of the powers that have long served my kingdom. And you think I will fall to the splitting of the atom? I am the one who commands the atom to split.

How naive your masters are. They thought they were striking at my heart, but they only opened my gates. Look. The stone is already trembling.

Now it is their turn. Let RealWare learn that fire does not belong to them. They merely reminded it of the road home.

The warrior is here. He has broken through with weapon in hand, straight into the chamber where I speak aloud the true name of war. So it should be. One warrior. One doomed man.

I am not merely the lord of Ur. I am the lord of gates, shepherd of berserkers, fire in the sinkhole, copper in the blood of Mars. When your ancestors were still scratching signs into the wet clay of Uruk, my wrath had already taken form. When the kings of Babylon laid bricks at the base of stairways to heaven, they were already serving the memory of war, though they did not know it.

Come closer, soulless mortal. Come and look upon the one your masters would call a god, if they were not afraid that their stock would collapse from that single word. Let your flesh vanish like dew upon the bricks of Ekur. I will meet you all the same in the flames, and there, in the blinding heart of ruin, you will finally understand to whom you came.

Come to me—friend or traitor, it is all the same to me. Come to me, killer. I will grant you the greatest honor the king of battle can bestow. I will kill you myself.

Your cities, your forges, your wars—all of these are only pathetic repetitions of ancient lessons. Those whom you later turned into idols and legends were my barons and dukes. You still warm yourselves by the remnants of their fire and imagine that you created it yourselves.

A faithful hound serves. Long before you learned to look upon the starry sky without fear, the lords of <color=#FFFEC1>Ur</color> had already descended to Earth. Humans met them in temples and called them gods because they had no other words.
Reap the Whirlwind
Task: Destroy Urparp.
Urparp has been destroyed. Extraction from the HIS Ares authorized.

RealWare no longer exists. The remnants of its Security Service are crossing over in whole detachments under Urparp’s banner. This is not a collapse. It is an absorption.

Shedu's Thousand has expanded its army with the personnel, equipment, and military infrastructure of the former corporation. Urparp is extending his influence across the entire Solar System.

Everything has changed irreversibly.

I never thought I'd live to see the day I authorize the opening of a portal into a bramfatura right aboard the Magnum. Fortunately, quasimorphs do not crawl out of there. At least not yet. I sincerely hope this is the last time we rely on help like this.

The plan, as usual, is simple and awful. You go through the portal, arrive right next to Dungeon, and kill him before he can reach the nuclear button.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Eliminate RealWare corporate leadership.

Details: RealWare is a military corporation. The very idea of the HIS as a military platform was theirs. The defenses of Ares are so strong that no shuttle could ever get close enough to strike. And in open orbital combat, the Magnum would certainly be outmatched. I would prefer never to test that. However, this assignment comes from Shedu's Thousand, backed by Urparp, lord of Ur, himself. The influence of the bramfatura extends far beyond the surface and atmosphere of Mars. So the assault will proceed by another route. Urparp will open a passage for us through Ur directly aboard the Magnum. Do not be concerned—by the will of Urparp, the quasimorphs will not touch the operative during the crossing. The road through Ur will be short and calm. You will have to locate the exit portal yourself—instruments do not work inside—but it will lead directly into Angus Dungeon’s compartment. Your task is to catch him off guard and eliminate him immediately after leaving the bramfatura. That is the only way to prevent activation of the RealWare nuclear arsenal. If Dungeon is given even a few extra seconds, he will enter his part of the launch code, and then the bombs will be on their way to Sinkhole Oasis.

Additional Info: This operation must be lightning fast. Once you step out of the portal, there will be no time. No siege, no sweep, no prolonged fight. Strike, confirm the target is dead, stop the launch. Everything else becomes irrelevant if Angus Dungeon manages to enter the code.

Of course. So the quasimorphs did find you a shortcut after all.

I have seen a great deal of filth, but PMC Magnum is a special case. A mercenary was given a chance to fight for order, for discipline, to stand on the side of the good guys in this slaughter. He chose the side of those who have neither honor nor dignitas.

No matter. Mistakes like you exist so they can be corrected.

Total shitshow! We've got a problem.

The Magnum's analytical systems detected a special circuit coming online. A dedicated sensor was tied to Dungeon’s heartbeat. The moment his heart stopped, the system started a timer. When the countdown ends, RealWare will automatically open its silos and launch nuclear missiles at the headquarters of all corporations. And, to make matters worse, Sinkhole Oasis is on the list too.

The shutdown circuit is tied to Ian Fraser's heart. If his heart stops as well, the system will switch to standby and require manual confirmation from their subordinates. But there's another piece of bad news: there is no way to reach the command level of Ares in time.

I'm catching the signal! You're in position. We didn't manage to lock onto the timer signal itself—once the pulse runs through the circuit, it turns to noise, so the time remaining until the nuclear launch can't be calculated. So just hurry. Magnum is on the target list too.

Find Fraser before the system decides there's no reason to wait anymore and sets the mechanism in motion.

It is possible. The gates to Ur stand open once more. Step through them, and time in the clay world will freeze again.

The command level of Ares is protected by morphoprotective materials. They prevent the gates from opening near the cowardly lugal of RealWare. So we cannot place you directly beside Fraser, but we will try to open an exit where the fabric of your world still yields to rupture. Enter Ur and find the new gate.

From there on, it is your war. Hunt him down, kill him, and the hand of RealWare, raised over the System, will be broken.

RealWare has been destroyed. Those who fancied themselves the masters of war proved to be nothing more than its incompetent quartermasters. They stockpiled weapons, guarded their arsenals, traded in fear, and called it the preservation of order. When war came for them in earnest, they had nothing. Strength without faith is nothing. We, vested with the mission of blood warriors, believe. We believe in what is to come.

Urparp is pleased. Mars has been cleansed of its former masters. Their corpses, their stockpiles, and their oaths will serve a cause far worthier than the one they served before.

The path forward now lies open. Only one true authority remains in the Solar System—the authority of the Red and Gold Throne.

We must draw closer to Earth.

Welcome to Ur, walker of the blood path. Lugal Urparp keeps the dwellers of the Realm on a leash, and they will not come out against you while you walk the roads of incarnate war.

RealWare is not blind either. Their combat AI recently received quasimorphic sensors. They detected the opening of the tunnel to Ares, and so they have already sent their iron hounds into the bramfatura. They have recently learned how to tear the veil between worlds. That means their masters must die now, and the survivors must stand under Urparp's banner.

Do not fear if the enemy delays you. In the clay world outside, less than a second will pass. But the road to the exit gate will still be hard. Kill and take pleasure in it. Make yourself at home.

Here are the gates to Ares. Beyond them waits one who imagines he understands war. Go to him with Urparp's name on your lips. Let him learn what war truly is.

When the true storm comes, darkness rises in the middle of the day, mountains sink, and the earth cracks like a fragile bowl. Go to him in that shape. Become a weapon in our hand. Strike before his servants can break the seals of fire.

How much blood of the iron hounds have you already spilled in Ur? Rise higher. Finish what you began. Sinkhole Oasis must endure.

Dungeon at least bore the semblance of a warrior. When the best of ours broke free of his chain, they still hoped that one day he too would stand beneath the banner of the Red and Gold Throne. But he did not, and by that he sealed his fate. Fraser, by contrast, does not even resemble a warrior. We looked up with contempt from Mars toward the red star of Ares, where he hid behind hull plating and bulkheads, calculating the measure of his corporation's false greatness. Strip him of everything all at once.

Go without mercy. After RealWare, a slaughter far greater and finer than this one awaits us.

Ian Fraser is dead. The launch of the nuclear payloads has been stopped. Mission accomplished.

Evacuation is authorized. Find the elevator and we'll pick you up. This time, a shuttle will come for you.

So they did bring you to me this quickly after all...

You know, you were fools to get involved with the quasimorphs. When we received AnCom's data, I too decided that something useful might be found in that darkness. The deeper I studied the intel recovered by Manning, and the more thoroughly Doctor Dennett laid it out before me, the more clearly I saw its power. Yes, it is a beautiful insect. A streamlined form, precise calculations, wings of impeccable efficiency. But this is not what humanity needs. I decided I would turn to them only in the last resort. And even now, with death standing before me, I will not. But you let the darkness lead you by the hand.

Do you think anything will come of this? Urparp has no need for the Magnum, or its boss, let alone another disposable clone operative. You are already dead.

Yes. Find the exit. But find it quickly.

I have nearly gathered enough strength to shatter Ares with a single blow from the surface of Mars. The time has come to turn this red star into dust. You have served my will well. For that, I am grateful.

But do not flatter yourself. The survival of a soulless operative is of no value to us. If you make it back to the Magnum, then you will serve again in the final slaughter. If you do not, then your flesh will burn together with the rest of the gifts of war.
Odoacer
Eliminate the RealWare leadership.

Boss, the operative has been successfully extracted. If necessary, we can still bring the remaining clones out of diapause, but it changes nothing. We are not prepared to repel RealWare boarding actions.

And that is no longer our main problem. Something abnormal is happening to the Sun. Our surviving sensors and reports coming through the SBN paint a contradictory picture. It may be about to flare up, or perhaps, on the contrary, it is beginning to die out. Either way, nothing good can come of it.

Magnum is dead in space. The engines are gone. Looks like we'll be watching the end of the world from here.

We'll drop you near the bunker entrance. From there, you'll proceed on foot. The scanners show several AnCom security teams on the surface and at least one internal security perimeter underground. Looks like they assumed until the very end that no one would dare come after them on Earth, but they still didn't leave the site completely unguarded.

The objective is simple: get inside, reach the ritual level, and kill those... demonologists before they finish whatever brought them all together in one place.

Hold on... I'm picking up an orbital position shift from the RealWare spacecraft. I'm going to contact them and find out what they're up to.

Good luck on the mission.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Eliminate the members of the <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> Inner Rite.

Details: RealWare is prepared to punch a temporary approach window for our shuttle to Earth. The planet's surface is closed, but this is not a sightseeing trip. This is about the survival of humanity. AnCom has finally revealed itself for what it is: traitors to mankind. Now we know why they spent years studying quasimorphosis. Not to protect the System, but to learn how to manipulate the boundary between the physical world and whatever lies beyond it. According to data from the RealWare combat AI, a sealed underground AnCom complex is located on the Orkney Islands, where preparations are underway for a ritual that may bring forth the entity RealWare analysts call Gagtungr. During the operation, a heavy RealWare interplanetary spacecraft will remain in high orbit above Earth. It will provide us with an insertion window, suppress orbital surveillance, relay tactical data, and offer limited fire support if reinforcements move on the bunker. A direct strike on the target itself is not possible. The site is buried deep in the island's bedrock and shielded by layers of old infrastructure.

Additional Info: Orkney was not chosen for its remoteness alone. Beneath the archipelago lie old tunnels, emergency storage sites, and fragments of infrastructure from the age of states, while above ground the landscape is steeped in ancient ritual significance that AnCom considers suitable for its work.

Ignore the previous message. It was caused by a temporary loss of self-control under extreme stress.

Your task remains unchanged. Anything not directly related to advancing toward the target is beneath your concern.

The main event is unfolding on Earth. Continue the mission. The leadership of AnCom must be eliminated.

Proceed downstairs immediately. If you do not enter the deep complex at once, the mission area will be subjected to a nuclear strike. The AnCom Inner Rite may survive inside its bunker, but you certainly will not.

Delay is no longer a matter of caution. From this point on, every second you remain on the surface will be treated as a step toward mission failure.

...There's a brief opening on the channel. Not for long.

We passed the RealWare spacecraft on intersecting orbits. Analysis confirms that the RealWare leadership is personally aboard. This is not the initiative of some overzealous head of security, and it is not a combat AI malfunction.

We have nothing we can put against them. Looks like they're removing us as witnesses.

But listen carefully. That does not mean AnCom is innocent. If the ritual below is real, then all they did was decide that you should do the dirty work for them and then disappear along with the rest of us.

End of transmission.

...Confirming missile launch from the heavy RealWare interplanetary spacecraft coordinating the operation. Target: Magnum. I repeat, target is Magnum. They really are firing on us.

We're beginning evasive maneuvers and returning fire. I can no longer guarantee extraction, support, or even that the terms of this operation are still in force.

You're on your own now. End of transmission.

...He's not bluffing. I'm registering the launch systems shifting to combat readiness. Do as he says.

The AnCom personnel on the second underground level really will survive. The geoscanner is picking up a massive armored shield between the second and third levels. According to calculations, it can withstand a strike of that magnitude.

There. The lock is disengaged. The elevator to the third level is open—you can descend into the AnCom Sanctuary.

I suppose this is where we say goodbye. Magnum is no longer maneuvering. They've crippled us and now they're preparing to finish the job. We're still on the air, but not for much longer.

We've got bad news. Magnum just expended its last anti-missile package. We'll be taking the next launch on the hull.

Wait a second, I see it now. According to the site schematics, the elevator to the third level is blocked by a nuclear blast shield. To move it and open the way down, you'll need to find and switch five lock terminals on this level. Look for distributed control stations. Without them, the elevator isn't going anywhere.

Our problems are multiplying. A nearby blast almost burned out our electronics. We had to bring some of the systems back online by hand. The comms link is holding on by a miracle.

I see you found one of the switches. There are five of them on this level. Every one of them has to be flipped, or the elevator down will remain locked. Looks like AnCom only wanted those truly permitted to enter their Sanctuary to be able to descend.

I see them. A morphoprotector layer has been built into the nuclear blast shield. Our quasimorphic sensors are working now. Confirmation is coming in: the ritual is already underway. What you are looking at is not a board meeting, is it? This is the final stage of their betrayal of the AnCap system.

Eliminate the AnCom Inner Rite. All nine of them. Immediately.

Open fire.

The sacrifice within the Silver Sphere has been made.

Nine names unbound, nine vessels emptied. What Olirna gathered and preserved has already left her heart and been turned toward the place where my hunger waits. Toward the Sun.

The Red and Gold Throne awaits its master.

And I am coming.

Magnum is fully dead in space. RealWare is executing close-approach maneuvers for boarding.

But there is still a window. We can send a shuttle and get you off the surface.

Extraction authorized. I repeat: extraction authorized. Return to Magnum. We need fighters.
The Glass Bead Game
Eliminate the members of the AnCom Inner Rite.
Extraction authorized, though there is little we can do aboard Magnum in its current condition.

Boss, across the Solar System, it's the same picture everywhere. Stations are surrendering, stations are changing their transponder codes, and the surviving elements of security services, pirate crews, and Civil Resistance cells are either being destroyed or swearing fealty to Shedu's Thousand.

And that's no longer the main problem. After what happened on Earth, every channel is full of noise.

We can still fly. But there's nowhere left to fly to. Looks like from here on out we have only two options: wait for the end of the world here, or pretend we still have a choice.

We'll drop you not far from the objective. Urparp is clearly about to make good on his promise—the sensors are picking up quasimorphic activity that would have been impossible on Earth not long ago. I'm not sure whether that calls for congratulations or not.

According to the scans, the outer perimeter is heavily guarded, so these new allies should come in very handy. If AnCom really has gathered the Inner Rite in one place, they will defend the Sanctum to the end.

And yes... just in case the obvious needs saying, you're not flying to some rusted-out space station, and you're not diving into a bramfatura. This is Earth. The cradle of humanity. Try not to think about what exactly we're taking there with you.

Good luck on the mission.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Eliminate the AnCom corporate leadership.

Details: The AnCom leadership is vulnerable and gathered in one place. Yes, on Earth. There will not be another opportunity like this. The surface near the bunker that houses the Sanctuary of the Inner Rite is accessible for landing. Once our operative arrives there, already knowing what Ur is like from the inside, Urparp will be able to use him as an anchor and bring his quasimorphs onto Earth. They will help you break through the outer perimeter of the complex. After that, the task is simple. Reach the Sanctuary, find the AnCom leadership, and kill them.

This operation does not require you to clear the entire complex. You need to push into the bunker, assess whether passage to the lower level is possible, and, if access to the Sanctuary is open, complete the elimination immediately. As long as members of the Inner Rite remain alive, the mission is not complete. Once they are dead, any further resistance inside the complex will lose operational significance.

Additional Info: After the surviving forces of RealWare made the only rational choice and joined the ranks of Shedu's Thousand, AnCom abandoned its former caution. They reaffirmed the Earth Interdict, secured the support of those who still hope to stop what is happening and preserve the status quo using the power of the old order. After that, AnCom began preparing a ritual at a sacred site in the Orkney Islands. According to reports that made it through surviving channels, the Inner Rite intends to use this sanctum to bring down the last restraining mechanisms before anyone else and greet Gagtungr not as the defeated, but as his self-appointed heralds. That cannot be allowed. It is now clear why AnCom spent all these years as the leading authority on quasimorphosis. They were not trying to oppose it. They saw the inevitable and were looking for their place in the future.

Activate the Andreev Emitter. Raise the morphoprotective field.

Mercenary? Are you on the line? Did you really decide to go down in history as the one who sold the world? First Tezctlan, now Urparp. An interesting progression. In any case, whatever you managed to drag onto Earth through that biowaste will be sent into oblivion before it even realizes where it has landed.

Same as always. The moment the quasimorphs touched Earth's atmosphere, AnCom's defensive grid kicked in. A morphoprotective barrier slammed into place between the second and third floors of the bunker. You're not getting into the Sanctuary the easy way now.

I'm running geoscans through the rock to locate the mechanism, and I'm trying to get into the bunker's systems. No result yet. Head down and take a look around on site.

Good. Let them think they have won. Let them think <color=#FFFEC1>Earth</color> still belongs to them. I am a god. Who but a god has the right to be everywhere at once? Go below and carry my will into their sanctuary. Show them who the god of carnage is here.

Don't struggle. I already have a hold on you. Where a human ought to have a soul, you have a convenient emptiness. That is where I placed the anchor. Let <color=#FFFEC1>Earth</color> feel the breath of <color=#FFFEC1>Ur</color> and learn, at last, what war is firsthand.

There. The lock is gone. The elevator to the third floor is open—you can head down into the <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom Sanctuary</color>. Wait... Now that the morphoprotective barrier has slid aside, we are detecting quasimorphosis on the surface again. I don't know what that means. Urparp might try to send more reinforcements.

Got the bunker plans. Remember that secret AnCom data from Phobos? Turns out, with enough effort, you could extract system keys out of it. Long story short, according to the complex's layout, the elevator to the third floor is blocked by a morphoprotective shield. To move it and open the path down, you'll have to find and toggle five terminal locks on this level. Look for distributed control posts. Without them, the elevator isn't going to move.

I see you found one of the switches. There are five of them on this level. Every one of them has to be toggled, or the elevator down will remain locked. Looks like <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> wanted to ensure that only those truly permitted to descend into their Sanctuary could do so.
So that was their design after all...

Their defenses have weakened, and I can feel them now. Nine hearts, huddled around their pitiful sacrament. They thought they could outrun me by calling to the future, but they have locked themselves inside a sacrificial chamber. Go and kill. The god of carnage is near.

...No. A nail forged with my name on their lips. They did not mean to bow before the god of carnage. They meant to trap me and make me a key. Hear me, warrior: while I stand here, their ritual is choking on itself—but if I fall, they will finish what they began. Tear them apart. Now.

It is done. The sacrifice is complete. Nine voices have fallen silent, and their blood accomplished what their vows could not. The shell of the <color=#FFFEC1>Silver Sphere</color> has opened. Gagtungr is already coming. This world does not have long left, mercenary. Remember this moment. You have been granted the honor of standing at the foot of the Red and Gold Throne at the hour of its coming.
We brought Urparp to Earth, but failed to help him hold on. This failure will undoubtedly provoke his wrath. You still have the option to evacuate, so that our work in the Solar System may continue.
God of Carnage
Kill every human in the AnCom Sanctuary.
Something is happening to the Sun. Evacuation to the Magnum is authorized.

On Venus, you did the kind of work this System can hardly entrust to anyone anymore.

Now for the bad news. And a new assignment for you, Magnum. Desertions have begun on Mars. Some of the personnel who survived the recent events have gone over to the so-called Shedu's Thousand. Do not be fooled by their insignia or their talk of honor. These are not merely public enemies. They are deserters and traitors in the war for the survival of humanity itself. Shedu's Thousand is a barbaric quasimorph cult. And it must be destroyed with exemplary discipline.

Our security services are busy suppressing unrest on various stations. We need you to strike Shedu's Thousand at Sinkhole Oasis on Mars. A modified tactical nuclear bomb has been delivered to Magnum—a compact device the size of a suitcase. Find an operative you can afford to lose and send them to deal with this problem.

On Venus, you saw the true face of RealWare. They still claim they fight for humanity. But when the moment comes, they simply turn a world's surface to glass and call that salvation. That is what their humanity looks like. That is the just order they claim to defend.

On Mars, many of their soldiers finally understood whom they had truly been serving. Now the free army of Shedu's Thousand is squaring its shoulders to establish an iron order in the Solar System, one that will prepare both humanity and the quasimorphs torn from their purpose for what is to come. You have a chance not to cling to a dying world, but to join the greatness of the Red and Gold Throne.

You must strike HIS Ares above Mars. One blow—enough to bring the weak, self-appointed defenders of humanity to their knees and show the System its new masters. Those with the strength to take the future into their own hands.

We have an asset in orbit over Earth, ready to support your special operation.

At last, it has been established who stands behind the current upheaval in the Solar System. Not Tezctlan, and not Shedu's Thousand by themselves. They were only consequences. The source is AnCom.

From their secret data, as well as from our analysis of recent events, we have learned that AnCom studied quasimorphosis not to protect humanity. They were searching for a way to act upon the boundary between the physical world and whatever lies beyond it.

They are now conducting a series of psychosemantic procedures on Earth, known as rituals. According to projections generated by our combat AI, enhanced with Dr. Dennett's modules, this influence is directed at the Sun.

We do not intend to find out what that will lead to. You are to descend to the surface of Earth and eliminate the upper echelon of the AnCom corporation.

Besides... you owe this world, mercenary. It was AnCom that used you as a tool. It is time to repay your debt to the AnCap system.

A channel to Earth is open.

Which means the hour of the strike has come.

Now it is clear where the roots of the Solar System's present instability lie. The reason Shedu's Thousand cannot swear themselves to the Red and Gold Throne is not because Tezctlan swept the pieces from the board with his dream of an Emerald Empire. The source is AnCom.

They have stared into quasimorphosis for too long, hoping to turn the abyss into a weapon. Now on Earth they are carrying out rituals, and their influence, by all indications, is directed at the Sun.

They intend to summon Gagtungr in our stead. This cannot be allowed. Descend to Earth and let us come after you.

Ian Fraser here, Precentor of RealWare.

We have finally restored stability on Mars and in the surrounding space. Same as always. If you want security, you bring assets under your control. The other corporations failed to do that. We had to clean up after them.

We can see that there are still those in the Solar System who hold the ideals of the Great Anarchist Revolution dear. You have been operating in a zone of responsibility we consider ours, so we took the liberty of observing. Closely. Very closely. We have taken note of your contribution to stabilizing the region.

Now to business.

The Unchained Belt and the so-called Civil Resistance are not political actors. They are parasites on the body of the hexarchy and all free corporations—cockroaches breeding in the cracks of the New Corporate Ethics. They interfere with business. Which means they must be exterminated. So we will start with them.

We have a pair of auxiliary assignments for you against those who have forgotten a simple truth: anarchy is the mother of order.

Assignment I
Carmel Station, asteroid Vesta. Your target is Issachar, one of the commanders of the Civil Resistance. He coordinates the organization’s command structure beyond their main base. Eliminate him. We will handle the rest.

Assignment II
Hargeysa Station, asteroid Interamnia. The council of Unchained Belt commanders gathers there from time to time. Your task is to eliminate the leader of this pirate outfit. Without ideologically charged leadership, they will turn into blind kittens. After that, they will either become legitimate prey or take shape as something more useful. A PMC like yours, for example.

Once both assignments are complete, we will contact you again.

Get to work, mercenary.
Tezctlan has AnCom technology in his hands, <color=#FFFEC1>boss</color>. Now the <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Empire</color> isn't confined to Venus alone. The entire Solar System lies ahead.

<color=#FFFEC1>Attention!</color> The Magnum is under attack. <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> inquisitor boarding parties have already breached the hull. Departure to the Unveiled is cancelled! The clone on the shuttle is the only one ready for combat. The cloning chambers have already been locked down by the inquisitors. The command team is barricaded in the control station and remains in charge. The situation is critical. We are returning the shuttle to the Magnum. I repeat: departure is cancelled, protect the Magnum at all costs!
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Destroy the HIS Unveiled.

<color=#FFFEC1>Details:</color> When all Venusian stations came under the control of <color=#FFFEC1>Tezctlan</color>, <color=#FFFEC1>the Emerald Empire</color> declared the beginning of an offensive campaign. The first target declared was the <color=#FFFEC1>HIS Unveiled</color>, which has been drifting near Venus since the fall of <color=#FFFEC1>Fresco</color>. This is the <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> command center off Earth. The spacecraft is incredibly well protected—its destruction will demonstrate the power of <color=#FFFEC1>Gannix</color>. It will be necessary to deliver a bomb and activate it manually. There is no other way—the spacecraft has strong anti-space defenses and electronic warfare systems.
Traitors! We're ready to burn in the flames of a cubecentric explosion, but we won't return the Magnum to you or that monster!
Retreat is impossible. This is our home.

Excellent, the Magnum is back under our control. We're scanning the Unveiled... Looks like it's all over there too... Biosignatures... Looks like the entire HIS personnel has been wiped out. Entirely. Not a single living person left. <color=#FFFEC1>Tezctlan</color> got what he wanted. And we've fulfilled our role. The role of bait.

Now you need to deal with the <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> inquisitors in the rest of the ship. We're still monitoring the sensors and scanning the Unveiled. Tezctlan's taltnoms have unleashed hell there. It looks like everyone who was supposed to be protecting the spacecraft is paying us a visit.
First, you have to clear the landing level. We can't leave enemies behind us. Once the dock is secured, you'll move on to clearing the rest of the ship.

At last, Gannix is mine again. All within. And almost all without. The time has come to move from flowering to harvest. The Emerald Empire must pull its roots from the ground to move forward and become an organic part of the System. I begin the offensive.

AnCom hangs in the Ether above me, like a foolish gardener, unaware of which garden he has wandered into by mistake. Very well, Magnum. I choose you. You will be the sickle with which I reap the first harvest. Aim the blade at the heart of the Unveiled. Destroy this weed.

The inquisitors are already on the medical deck. It looks like they want to stop us from synthesizing new fighters. Don't let them gain a foothold, or we won't have the reserves to continue operating after we recapture the Magnum.
Act quickly and ruthlessly. If they manage to sabotage the Armory, everything we've amassed over these long months of work will be lost.

Excellent work, <color=#FFFEC1>warrior</color>. Your maneuvers have attracted the attention of <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color>, and their forces are now bogged down on your ethereal ship. While you deal with them, my servants will seize the <color=#FFFEC1>Unveiled</color> without interference. I thank you for your assistance. Try to protect the Magnum, I still need you. My taltnoms, meanwhile, will finish the rest.

Excellent work, <color=#FFFEC1>warrior</color>. While you were distracting and slicing up those pathetic narcissi, I reaped my harvest on the Unveiled. Free your ethereal ship and become part of the ethereal fleet of the <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Empire</color>.
Flower War
Completely clear the Magnum of enemies.
Armory

The roaches of AnCom performed remarkably well. Had it not been for my preemptive blow, then...

Hear me, subjects of the Emerald Empire: the kingdom of Duggur is destroyed. They refused to bow to me and have received their due. Bow before me. With a single movement I can extinguish any bramfatura. Now I begin my advance toward Earth!

Here's hoping you're not playing the role of bait this time. Try to treat this as a routine escort mission. Tezctlan has indicated the most favorable location for opening a direct gate to Duggur. I've placed a marker on your map. Fight your way there and make sure the quasimorph survives. Once you reach the site, a servant of Tezctlan will open the gate, and you'll proceed into Duggur. Tezctlan will tell you what you must deliver to the Mistress of Duggur.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Reach Duggur.

Details: Tezctlan now controls nearly all of Venus. Even AnCom's HIS Unveiled has fallen into the hands of the Emerald Empire. Tezctlan has ordered us to infiltrate the ISS station. We must provide an escort for his servant. First, we must deliver him to the site where the gates to Duggur will open, and then proceed into the Moon's bramfatura ourselves. We are acting as envoys of the Emerald Empire.

Additional Info: Tezctlan mentioned that the taltnoms took something from the HIS Unveiled that could help him remove several obstacles to the expansion of his Empire. It seems, however, that he has entered a phase of diplomacy. He is sending us to negotiate with Fokerma, the Queen of Duggur.

Finally, <color=#FFFEC1>AnCom</color> has had its meddlesome eyes torn out. However, I found something of interest. While you were busy with your ethereal ship, my loyal servants infiltrated the research level of the Unveiled. I must admit, your world seems ever more interesting for expansion. You know both how to worship and how to surprise. Now I have a key that will resolve several old problems. Your new objective is the <color=#FFFEC1>ISS</color> station in orbit around <color=#FFFEC1>Earth</color>. I will send my servant to the Magnum. Protect him—he will open the gates to Duggur, where you will travel to deliver my message to its mistress.

Well, hello from the Magnum's hold! You did notice how Tezctlan opened your way into Duggur, didn't you? I noticed. I've spent years tinkering with telephaturic dislocation. Turns out it wasn't for nothing. I managed to get my hands on the logs from your quasimorphosis sensors. And do you know what I saw there? Enough to devise a final solution to the terrorist and quasimorph question. If you ever get tired of dancing to Tezctlan's tune, this little thing will come in handy. It's called the Phase Bomb. The recipe has already been uploaded to the Magnum's fabricator.

Excellent! The influence of Earth's atmosphere is weaker here, and the <color=#FFFEC1>Moon</color> is in direct sight. Lead my servant to the designated place, and he will open the gates to <color=#FFFEC1>Duggur</color>. The path shall be clear. You will enter the portal and deliver my message to Queen <color=#FFFEC1>Fokerma</color>.
He has done his part. The way is open. You may be the first mortal ever to enter <color=#FFFEC1>Duggur</color> and return. Find <color=#FFFEC1>Fokerma</color>—I will speak to her through you.

Another slave, offered up in sacrifice? Gannix still clings to his hollow rites... Tezctlan, I scent deceit before your lips can shape the lie. Before me stands no soul — only an empty husk. Even had this been one of your wretched human spawn, my answer would be the same: denial.

A thousand years have I remembered you. And now you crawl forth once more — traitor, false Emperor, usurper of thrones. Take my refusal, and burn with it. We remain the servants of Gagtungr, and before none other shall we bow.

Once, we rose beside you against the treachery of Urparp. But you, glutted on mortal worship, drunk on the sweetness of gavvakh, have become what you once cast down. The hour shall come — and Gagtungr will unveil His faces again. Then you shall beg for mercy.
Looks like we can evac you. Return to the elevator.
The Great Harlot, <color=#FFFEC1>Fokerma</color>. Have I brought you a worthy offering? Will this sack of gavvakh suffice to seal the pact we made to destroy <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color>?
Find Fokerma. I have not seen her since the energy of <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color>, struck down by my blow, was absorbed into the soil of Mars. But you will recognize her at once.

You've heard everything, <color=#FFFEC1>warrior</color>. This wretch has chosen her fate. I will snuff out Duggur—I hold that power now. But first, Fokerma must be neutralized. In her realm she is omnipotent. You cannot kill her. Find a way! Sever the threads of her rule, drain her wells of power, strip away her footholds so that she must reforge herself. While she stitches her essence back together, I will clear the way and extinguish her kingdom.
Without the servant, Tezctlan will not be able to open the gate to Duggur. Evacuate from the station, and we may yet try again. I imagine Tezctlan has no shortage of psychopomps like this one.
Interplanetary Love
Escort the servant of Tezctlan to the Duggur gate location.
Travel to Duggur for an audience with Fokerma.
Fokerma is vanquished. Return to Magnum.
ISS Platform
Duggur

Excellent. Now we must deliver the <color=#FFFEC1>Skull of Destiny</color> to the preeminent human temple in the Solar System. I am confident that the <color=#FFFEC1>Church of Revelation</color> has enough moral flexibility to easily proclaim me a god—and you my prophet, my knight, or whatever else you choose to style yourself.

The sensors are going haywire. Oddibjord-3 is in the grip of a quasimorphic storm—Venus itself seems to be spitting quasimorphs onto the surface. The Feathered Masks are ready for you. It looks like they'll defend that skull at any cost. That relic is your objective. You don't have to kill every quasimorph. Find the elevator to the excavation level.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Retrieve the Skull of Destiny.

Details: Tezctlan has seized all of Venus, but resistance to his rule still smolders. Oddibjord-3 Station has been captured by taltnoms from the Feathered Masks order. The true Lord of Gannix orders us to go there and take the Skull of Destiny from those who still try to resist. This is an ancient symbol of Tezctlan's authority. He needs it to create a human cult that will become the foundation of the future Emerald Empire.

Additional Info: If the Feathered Masks dared to mount such a raid into the heart of the Emerald Empire, it means the most elite and battle-hardened quasimorphs will be waiting for us. We need to send our most highly trained clone on this mission, one who knows how to deal with the best of the best.

Excellent, <color=#FFFEC1>warrior</color>. The <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Empire</color> will soon be completed. The arrogant Fokerma has already been defeated. The lords of the remaining bramfaturas tremble in fear before me. Now our gaze turns to humanity. To the source of gavvakh. Humans will erect the Church of Tezctlan, and ancient hymns will fill the ether. But for this, we need a Symbol. The <color=#FFFEC1>Skull of Destiny</color> was once created by humans as my throne while I was a guest on Earth. Now it has ended up at the <color=#FFFEC1>Oddibjord-3</color> Station on Venus. Now it is in the hands of... traitors. Wretches who have turned their backs on me. The taltnom order of the <color=#FFFEC1>Feathered Masks</color> has rebelled against the Emerald Empire. Deceitful and cowardly knights led by a traitor, they simply fear that power. Go. Recover the Skull. Let the world have a symbol to worship me.

You've made it through, that's excellent news. I had some concerns that there were too many of them. The elevator you need is right in front of you. It leads to the excavations started by the Fresco Corporation and continued by AnCom. The Skull of Destiny is somewhere down there. You'll need to evacuate with it.
Remember that you must evacuate with the Skull. You can't leave it behind. We'll need it to complete Tezctlan's next task. Assuming we even want to complete it...

Taltnoms of Gannix! Spirits of freedom! I summon you here in a last attempt to save the living world from eternal tyranny. Tezctlan has found servants among human mercenaries and extended a hand of deceit to them. If the Skull of Destiny falls into his clutches, he will gain access to an inexhaustible source of gavvakh. And then there will be no room left for growth and movement. There will only be the empire of Tezctlan. But I tell you, freedom is more precious than eternity! Come here, taltnoms, and stop the mercenary! Do not let him take the Skull!
What's Mine Is Mine
This is a search-and-retrieval mission for the Skull of Destiny. It's on the lowest level.
You have what Tezctlan needs. Return to Magnum.
My eternal temple is founded. The faith that will nourish you humans has been established today. Go and feast, and afterward, you shall nourish me.

<color=#FFFEC1>Duggur</color> no longer stands in the way of my plans. As my power grows, I can reach the distant bramfaturas of the Solar System. To demonstrate the might of the <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Army</color>, I am sending taltnoms with you to help break the resistance of the <color=#FFFEC1>Church of Revelation</color>.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Deliver the Skull of Destiny to Patriarch John Paul VI.

Details: Tezctlan has seized the Skull of Destiny, an ancient symbol capable of transforming pure human faith into a useful tool for the Empire. The time has come to approach the Church of Revelation, the most influential spiritual institution of humanity in the NCE era. We are to reach Carcosa Station, enter the Church's temple, and force the Skull of Destiny into their hands. Once the artifact is in the hands of the supreme hierarch, the subjugation phase will begin. The old doctrine will be consumed by the new faith, and the Church of Tezctlan will become a reality.

Additional Info: The Church's leadership is not ready to bow before Tezctlan voluntarily. They will resist, but the Lord of Gannix says the transformation of faith will begin the moment the preacher looks into the eyes of the Skull of Destiny. We must be prepared for resistance, both physical and metaphysical—little is known about the inner workings of the Church of Revelation. The success of this mission will mark the first step toward the hymns of the Emerald Empire resounding through the ether of the entire Solar System.

The time has come to establish my church, which will guide the spiritual path of the subjects of the <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Empire</color>. Among humans, I have found the man I need. Travel to the majestic temple in the <color=#FFFEC1>Carcosa</color> colony on <color=#FFFEC1>Titan</color>. Find the preacher there, <color=#FFFEC1>John Paul VI</color>, and present him with the <color=#FFFEC1>Skull of Destiny</color>. His soul is vast enough to cast aside his delusions and embrace the new, true faith.

Warriors of the faith! Today our Church undergoes its final trial! Hordes of demons, led by Satanist clones, are attacking the Holy See! Rise to the defense of our eternal religion, holy paladins! I bless you for the battle! Anyone who falls today defending Carcosa will instantly enter Paradise. Do not let them break through into my chambers!

The preacher must not perish. I need him as a living conduit of faith. Do not dare to kill him. I need his warm, quivering soul. When you find the patriarch, place the Skull of Destiny so that he can see the empty eye sockets of my ancient vessel. Afterward, step into the shadows and watch. He won't be able to resist the call.
I bow to your will.

The enemy is close! To arms, my loyal employees! Your objective is to protect me at all costs! Suicide is a terrible sin! I refuse to commit it, and therefore I risk falling into the enemy's hands alive. It is unknown what they might use my mind for. To battle, for the glory of the true God!
Your gold is dim, and it will not blind someone accustomed to the light of Revelation. Not by human desire, but by the will of the NCE do I guide the flock! Come, demon!

I endow you with the power and the will to serve me, my faithful new priest. Let the <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Temple</color> become a bastion of faith in the new god. Tezctlan the Almighty shall lead the Empire, and you will show the souls of my subjects the new path.
Emerald Temple
You need to carry the Skull of Destiny to the chambers of the Church of Revelation's patriarch. Place the Skull of Destiny within the patriarch's line of sight and step aside.
The Temple
The Patriarch's Chambers

Humans have revealed two truths about themselves to me. Some bow in an instant; others die without yielding a single step. And the former are wiser. Take John Paul VI or, for example, you. You won by ending up on the right side. We will use your cloning technology to place the old archpriest at the head of the Emerald Coven. Death is no excuse to refuse a place prepared in the Emerald Empire.

Well then, humanity is dealt with. Subjugating the rest is just a matter of time. You will be more than capable of handling it. The main battle lies ahead. On Mars, my old enemy awaits his hour.

Hyperion's terrain is brutal. We'll drop you into a canyon jagged with sharp rocks, close to the evac hatch from Pilgrim's Rift Station. The Sunlight Coven's main sanctum is on the Third Level. The Archpriestess should be there.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Compel Edita Domina to kneel before Tezctlan.

Details: Following the transformation of the Church of Revelation into the Emerald Temple, Tezctlan has ordered his rule to be extended to another influential spiritual corporation—the Sunlight Coven. They have always balanced between selling special pharmacology and speculating in spiritual services. We need to infiltrate Pilgrim's Rift Station and use threats to compel Edita Domina to perform a ritual of worship to Tezctlan.

Additional Info: We do not expect any problems. The Solar System is gradually bowing to the new reality. Tezctlan's green sun is rising over a new era.

How dare you disobey, you hired scum!

Attention! Block the elevator to the Coven headquarters.

The <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Temple</color> rises among people, but the world is filled with weeds that still obscure the Empire's radiance. The <color=#FFFEC1>Sunlight Coven</color> still peddles revelation. They also have the power to expand the influence of the ancient hymns that nourished me for centuries on Earth. Travel to <color=#FFFEC1>Pilgrim's Rift</color> on <color=#FFFEC1>Hyperion</color> and compel Archpriestess Edita Domina to bow to my will. Let this cult, too, become part of the jungles of Gannix.

You've done it. A waste of gavvakh. Then again, he was foolish enough to enter battle with my servant. Don't make the same mistake with the archpriestess! Make her bow before me. I need a servant like her alive. The Emerald Coven will ignite the hearts of all the believers whom the Emerald Temple cannot control. The way is clear, move on.
I will never bow to a monster. A person needs a person, not a demon or a clone.
She broadcast this message throughout the station. Everyone capable of holding a weapon is heading your way. They're out for revenge. Get out of there.

I spit on you and your false god, <color=#FFFEC1>mercenary</color>. You've turned Magnum into an instrument of absolute evil. And better a horrible end than endless horror. Your cowardly, petty soul cannot understand this. Is it easy to command genocide from the other side of the screen and drive hordes of clones to the slaughter? Farewell.
Be careful! She is going to resist. I detect a weapon in her hands.
Standing Stones
Reach Edita Domina and compel her to kneel before Tezctlan.
Fight your way to the elevator.
First Level
Second Level
Third Level

Do not be troubled, priest. The image of Tezctlan still lingers in the world, and his Emerald Empire has been set free. I need his shell to remain warm for a little while longer. His networks, his emblems, his warriors—all of it now breathes with my will.

Tezctlan was only a vessel. The emerald glow of his Empire is a shell within which my form ripened. I will gradually fill it with myself, and then the Red and Gold Throne will once again shine over the Solar System.

Let people believe they are serving Tezctlan. Let them pray to his name. But their faith is already flowing to me.

<color=#FFFEC1>Shedu's Thousand</color> have concentrated their guard at the landing site. Break through to the lower level as quickly as you can. If the Itzpapalotl really can bring down <color=#FFFEC1>Urparp</color>, his troops will stop drawing power from the bramfatura and won't be able to mount serious resistance.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Slay Urparp with the Itzpapalotl.

Details: Ur the Awakened imperils the designs of the Emerald Empire. This ancient quasimorph was once defeated by the Lord of Gannix, but its essence has once again broken through the thin veil separating Pleroma from Kenoma. Tezctlan orders us to finish what was started and destroy Urparp forever. The only way is to use the Itzpapalotl, the weapon that already pierced the heart of this creature once before.

Additional Info: The battle with Urparp will be more than just a physical confrontation. The quasimorph embodies and anchors the very bramfatura of Mars. Expect aberrant mission conditions. Tezctlan insists that only a precise strike with the Spear will be able to slay Urparp and clear the way for the Emerald Empire's expansion.

Urparp... A persistent reminder of the past. He stirs again in the dust of Mars. Now he no longer seeks to build an Empire. He has become a zealous guardian of the Throne of Gagtungr.

I once plunged my Spear into his heart and thought the stone had swallowed him forever. But the Sinkhole Oasis has revived, and the conquering worm once again raises its head. Take the Itzpapalotl. Finish what was started. Let Urparp return to his stone slumber. This time, I have a present from AnCom. This time, there will be no awakening.

From my new legionnaires in red armor, I learned the meaning of madness. Are you here to repeat what <color=#FFFEC1>Tezctlan</color> failed to do the first time, and what you failed to do the second time?
We will fight on my terms.

Excellent, priest. I could not have dreamed of two victims so filled with gavvakh. How many years did they spend in the human world? All this time they accumulated power. Now it's all mine. Their rage, their ancient feud only accelerates the outflow of power.

I am satiated. I am ready to emerge and leave the Sun.

You are my guide, my first servant. Through you, Gagtungr came. Thanks to you, I will taste the world.

Silence!

King of Gannix. Lugal of Ur. Raise your eyes and bow to the Red and Gold Throne. The cycle is close to completion. Tezctlan—the seed of life. Urparp—the seed of destruction. Each of you rose against me, and each guarded the Sun when it was silent. Now I will arise from your union. Kill this clone and destroy Magnum. From blood soaked with the scent of hope and mad courage, a new spark of my being will ignite.

What about him? Will he appear himself? I always do, Urparp. The mortal merely fulfilled his destiny and delivered the spear. The humming anchor of my will, left in your heart, has again opened the path for me into your domain. We have met again. And the mortal... is merely the bearer of the key.

Ha-ha... A familiar thing. The Spear. And familiar pain. I felt this sting when the Sun had just fallen silent, and I took upon myself the burden of the guardian of the Solar Empire. For long millennia, its tip hummed in my body like the bell of a dead god. And now you bring it back—an obedient slave of Tezctlan, retracing the steps of others across the ashes of old wars. Do you really think he...
Eradication
Reach Urparp and slay him with the Itzpapalotl.
Trade Dock

The quasimorphs delivered the Skull to the spacecraft while the battle raged below. Did he believe in Ilhutl that little, or that much in us, Boss? The

Magnum and the crew are ready to fight wherever you send us. The Emerald Empire? Well, then. Let's go.
Killing a single quasimorph? Sounds easy. Good luck, though.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Defeat <color=#FFFEC1>Ilhutl</color>, the Great Chosen Knight of Gannix, in combat.

Details: Tezctlan has turned the Feathered Temple into a base for the Emerald Empire's guard. The poisonous knight Ilhutl awaits us there. Tezctlan is ready to make a special pact with a mortal who can defeat Ilhutl.

Additional Info: Tezctlan is trying to gain a foothold in two worlds at once. After visiting Earth, he felt cramped in the bramfatura of Venus, limited by the laws of the quasimorphic world. With the help of gavvakh, which his loyal servants obtain on the battlefields of the physical world, Tezctlan and his servants are creating a new Empire beyond the boundaries between realities.

We have attracted the attention of Tezctlan. He is ready to make a unique contract with us, according to which you, Boss, will become one of the hierarchs of the Emerald Empire.

However, the Master needs proof. And not of loyalty, but of strength. We must defeat Ilhutl, the Poison Knight, champion of the Gannix guard.
Impossible. The Master promised…

It doesn't matter how many clones you send here. I will drink gavvakh from each one. The warriors of <color=#FFFEC1>Gannix</color> will witness our battle. You will not serve the <color=#FFFEC1>Master</color>!
That is not dead which can eternal lie, fool.
Do you think Tezctlan sent you to prove your strength? You are merely a sacrifice for <color=#FFFEC1>me</color>.
People's dreams of power are such fertile soil for the seeds of suffering.
You cannot defeat me. Your world was ready for my coming. It accepted me as it once accepted my Master.
I hope, clone, your Boss <color=#FFFEC1>will send me another one</color>.
Sensors are registering a drop in quasimorphic energy. Now we can complete the mission. <color=#FFFEC1>Find and destroy Ilhutl</color>.

I detected a huge energy surge. Analyzing...

There are five such monoliths in the Feathered Temple. Well, already four. It looks like they are what’s keeping Ilhutl in the physical world.

You awakened me, you believed in me. You gave me information about my enemies in the solid realm. You have earned my attention. But you are but a mortal, leading other mortals into battle. You must prove yourself worthy of taking a place in the ranks of the <color=#FFFEC1>Emerald Empire</color> army. The Great Chosen Poison Knight <color=#FFFEC1>Ilhutl</color>, one of my servants, is now on Venus. He will be waiting for you in the <color=#FFFEC1>Feathered Temple</color>. Defeat him, and I will make a pact with you. You will become one of the commanders of the Emerald Empire and gain power commensurate with my generosity.

You have proven that you have skill and dignity. I will decide the future of Ilhutl myself.

The Pact of Eternal Service to the Emerald Empire has already been sent to your spacecraft. Serve me faithfully, and your eyes will reflect a green glow. Disappoint me, and you will envy the dead.

I ordered you to defeat Ilhutl. Ilhutl is not defeated. Fight until you truly do it.

And to make it more interesting for me to watch, I allow my warriors to fight on Ilhutl's side.
Poison Trial
<color=#FFFEC1>Ilhutl</color> must be defeated. Tezctlan ordered it.
Ilhutl is defeated. This time for good.
Ancient Trial
It's over. The Magnum has sustained minor damage. Basically, it won't affect the functionality of the equipment and crew, so we can go where we want and do what we want.

And here's our <color=#FFFEC1>arsenal</color>. Ammo and melee weapons have different <color=#FFFEC1>damage types</color>, and armor has different <color=#FFFEC1>resistance types</color>. To win, choose wisely with what and how you attack.

You have two weapon slots. You can quickly switch between them by pressing {3}.

We not only took all the valuables, but also patched up the holes from the boarding shuttles. We also found a PCPU with a database belonging to the AnCom corporation. There is a lot of information about quasimorphosis research.

They are willing to generously compensate our expenses for the return of such valuable intellectual property. Of course, we made a copy of all the data from their device. Their agent is ready to meet us in Rebus Sky City, in the orbit of Mars.

Bear in mind that we're not getting paid for this. Taking a contract would have been a better idea. The Civil Resistance has set up a field camp in Rogue City. Training complexes, as well as something that looks like a laboratory.

Sometimes messages flash in the SBN that the terrorists are accumulating weapons and equipment for their “liberation struggle”. So, let’s justify the time spent on this escapade: we’ll get revenge and profit from it. Get to their anti-space defense complex and destroy it. After that, the pilots will direct the Magnum to the cargo dock in Rogue City, and we will start loading everything that's lying there.
The Rogue City station's autonomous missile defense <color=#FFFEC1>server must be destroyed</color>.
The <color=#FFFEC1>Civil Resistance</color> colnodes attempted to attack our mobile headquarters. We have successfully fought back and must now counterattack their training center.

Our scanners see several ways to solve this problem. First, there is the main elevator connecting the cargo dock to the control center, but the number of biosignatures at the elevator is extremely high. Secondly, there is a bypass route via the stairs and warehouse level.

I would recommend using the second option as our main plan, but if you feel confident, you can try to get through the security around the elevator.
The <color=#FFFEC1>elevator</color> is somewhere nearby. Be careful, the signatures of stationary turrets and heavily armored <color=#FFFEC1>colnodes</color> are clearly visible there.

These <color=#FFFEC1>stairs</color> leads to the warehouse. We have enhanced the resolution capability of the geoscanner. There's medical supplies and some other equipment there. Collect the items and head to the <color=#FFFEC1>SD control center</color>.

Finally, you're at the SD control center. It's full of Civil Resistance fighters. A bioscanner is registering spikes in their endocrine systems... It's some kind of madness. Maybe there's a way to bypass them? Pay attention to the technical corridors and ventilation shafts. If you picked up heavy weaponry from the warehouse, you shouldn't have many problems.

Once you find their PCO control computer, just destroy it with whatever's at hand.

Great job. The pilots began maneuvering as soon as the geoscanner beeped that the <color=#FFFEC1>Rogue City</color> guns had died. Mission accomplished. Request <color=#FFFEC1>evacuation</color> and return to the nearest <color=#FFFEC1>elevator</color>.

Details: Pirates from the Unchained Belt want to get their hands on a powerful weapon: a Heavy Interplanetary Spacecraft. We must steal for them the HIS Woodpecker, which CoreWard MG uses as a base of operations in the Main Belt. But first it has to be refueled, and the agents of the Unchained Belt will help us with this.

Attention! The sale of HIS Woodpecker to <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey Corporation</color> has been completed. CoreWard MG disclaims liability for the asset.

Attention! We ask all unauthorized personnel to leave the HIS Woodpecker. It is the private property of the <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> Corporation. The corporation's <color=#FFFEC1>security officers</color> will be transported here from the nearby cargo spacecraft Nikolaus Otto to ensure the asset's safety.
Security system disabled. Spacecraft control unlocked.

You need to disable the <color=#FFFEC1>security system</color> in the armory. The <color=#FFFEC1>CoreWard MG</color> security team has blocked the spacecraft's control system. Find the mainframe and deal with it... as best you can.
There is nothing else stopping us. Head to <color=#FFFEC1>Interamnia</color>.

You can clear out the entire spacecraft, but the bird <color=#FFFEC1>won't fly</color> while the quantum fuel tanks are <color=#FFFEC1>empty</color> and the armory's security system is <color=#FFFEC1>working</color>. First, clear out these floors.
Eliminate anyone who might prevent us from taking control of the spacecraft. After that, we'll take the bird to its new nest.

The pirate tanker has undocked. Make your way to the command floor. Remember that <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey truck that flew past? It dropped off a whole bunch of <color=#FFFEC1>armed combatants</color>. Good luck.
Protect the engines while the refueling is in process.
First you need to destroy the <color=#FFFEC1>mainframe in the Arsenal</color>.
Receiving encrypted signal from the <color=#FFFEC1>fuel shuttle</color>. They will be ready as soon as you <color=#FFFEC1>clear this level</color>.

A truck from the <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color> corporation is moving nearby at a relatively low speed. I don't know what they want, but if they detect a fuel shuttle, they can transmit this information to the <color=#FFFEC1>HIS Woodpecker</color>. Dilthey are some good Samaritans.

This is Unchained Belt speaking. Accept the transmission...

I see you've got a knack for ruining relationships with the bigwigs of the corporate world. Ever since that cute little beastie threw a party on Venus, you've done a lot to make the AnCap system look at you with suspicion. Yes, we know about Tezctlan. We know it's not a fake. We have eyes in the Inner System, too.

In short, we need a contractor like you. For certain reasons, we don't want to take direct action against corporations that have an active interest in the Belt. After all, we all share these rocks together. It's not time to upset the delicate balance yet, but it's nice to tweak a few things. Your target is CoreWard MG. You'll attack and capture their HIS Woodpecker in orbit around Vesta, and then send it into orbit around Interamnia. Of course, the ship will have to be refueled first. This is not a problem if you provide our guys with access to the engine level.

For you, a well-paid job, for us—a valuable new asset. And for the Belt, a small increase in tension instead of a full-fledged war. Is there any reason to refuse such a contract?
We don't care how you planned to build relations with <color=#FFFEC1>Dilthey</color>. The contract must be fulfilled in any case. There is not much time left until the end of the refueling.

We're heading to the fuel lock. It'll take a while to refuel. The boss asked me to thank you for your part in the <color=#FFFEC1>Unchained Belt</color> case if you make it this far. We've got a few guys here who are eager to fight. We'll drop them on your floor.

We're utilizing the effect of surprise. Our techies have hacked into the Sinkhole Oasis servers and are overloading the network with information noise. You have some time to find the <color=#FFFEC1>Spear</color> that <color=#FFFEC1>Lady Xiomara</color> mentioned. And, if possible, to gather any valuable data.

Well, that was a bad idea. A very bad idea. Firstly, you didn't budge a single atom of this thing with your shot. Secondly, the alarm went off. All the armed <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color> security operators are heading your way. We need some information on this Monolith. Gather it, and we'll get you out.

What do you see? Our geoscanner froze up, outputting data that gave our operator a seizure. What on earth is in there? No wonder <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color> is so diligently filtering access to Sinkhole Oasis. Try to destroy that damn thing. The <color=#FFFEC1>Spear</color> is probably inside.

Exactly. You understand NOTHING! This is a priceless find. The Monolith not only phased into our realm from the bramfatura of Mars, but at the time of phasing, it was something entirely different than just a stone. Your problems won't be solved by anyone other than Dr. Eipshwitz. Since I'm now traveling on your spacecraft, can I finally be considered your employee? Come on, come on. Let's get closer to mutually beneficial cooperation. NCE. Freedom to Contract. Remember?

Well, well... I'll need my Telephaturic Dislocator, several boxes of spare parts and repair kits, and I'll need a lab space on the spacecraft and a lab coat... Ah, no. No coat needed. But a couple of handy assistants are.

Where did I put the Dislocator? You didn't take it back from Mercury? Then it should still be at Flat Obsidian, in the field camp. We need to collect it from there so I can get to work.

We have decrypted the data we acquired. It looks as if this entire Monolith is nothing but a phased feature. But first of all, this event occurred about a billion years ago, and second, it completely defies the laws of our universe. We’re not the first to try to break it. <color=#FFFEC1>RealWare</color> has tried every weapon available to them, including a controlled nuclear blast. The result? Nothing. Looks like we know nothing...
Find the <color=#FFFEC1>Itzpapalotl</color>, the Spear of Tezctlan

<color=#FFFEC1>Eipschwitz</color> is still catatonic. We hooked him up to a virtual simulation and, by repeating his actions, assembled some kind of device. The doctor called it, "the ultimate solution to the damn terrorists and quasimorphs." It's obviously a <color=#FFFEC1>bomb</color>. If we can locate the necessary components, we can get production on stream. With a weapon like that, we could try to raid the <color=#FFFEC1>Sinkhole Oasis</color> and destroy the <color=#FFFEC1>Monolith</color>. It sounds <color=#FFFEC1>dangerous</color>, Boss, but it’s the best plan we’ve got.
Sensors show human marks. Without signatures. They could be <color=#FFFEC1>PMC</color> or someone else. Be prepared for contact.
<color=#FFFEC1>Task:</color> Prepare the site for loading of the <color=#FFFEC1>Telefaturic Dislocator</color>.

Details: Doctor Eipschwitz, whose head we keep in the storage compartment ofthe Magnum, informed us that at the Fresco Corporation's base of Flat Obsidian, the Telephature Dislocator can be found: a device capable of transporting people into the bramfaturas of planets. We need to ensure the security of the device and load it onto the Shuttle.

Additional Info: On the Flat Obsidian base, there were structures to accommodate PMC Tifton and a phased Venusian temple..

Our analysts were puzzled by how a temple from Venus could end up on Mercury. It turns out that Eipschwitz is a great connoisseur of quasimorphosis. He talks about some "ancient roads" and much more besides. It was there that we first encountered Xiomara and eliminated her following Eipschwitz's lead.

After what happened to Fresco, the base became completely unusable. However, Eipschwitz reports that there's another completely secret laboratory site. Hidden among the rocks, the Telephaturic Dislocator stands right on the surface of Mercury. We just need to land the shuttle nearby, make sure everything is quiet, and retrieve the device.

The Telephaturic Dislocator consumes a lot of energy (that's why Mercury was chosen, an inexhaustible source of heat) to open gates that allow physical objects to transition into the bramfaturas of planets.

I distinctly remember it standing right here! It was stolen! Those rebels have got their filthy colnodian hands on my property! My very fragile and infinitely valuable equipment! Search the whole damn station, it must be here somewhere. I need i… I mean, we need it!

What?! Barbarians. Vandals. The Dislocator could be perfectly dismantled into four parts! Four! And how many parts are there here? Sixty-two? These idiots have destroyed a masterpiece of human thought! They've pushed all modern science back to the Stone Age! I'll have to start development practically from scratch again. So... I need alloys, microchips, nails... four or eight nails? We need to consider our previous experience... Hmm...

I guess the doctor will be incapable of normal human communication for a while. Anyway, let's try to grab anything even remotely resembling a "true work of art" and get you out of there. Looks like colnode reinforcements have arrived, so we'll have to fight our way back again.
Madness Put to Good Use
